docs.title: Entity indexer concurrency
docs.text:
Use this reference when multiple threads or processes can access zettelforge.entity_indexer.EntityIndexer. ZettelForge 2.8.0 serializes in-process mutations and creates atomic file snapshots. Concurrent lookup safety is still in progress: search_entities() and stats() can fail while another thread mutates the index.

Module: zettelforge.entity_indexer Verified release: ZettelForge 2.8.0

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Install ZettelForge 2.8.0 on Python 3.10 or newer. Start with the Quickstart if you do not have a working installation.
  • Treat one EntityIndexer instance as shared mutable state when threads use it.
  • Coordinate separate processes outside ZettelForge. Its file lock does not serialize processes that write the same index path.

Concurrent lookup safety is in progress

Do not call search_entities(), stats(), or build() at the same time as a mutation. A release-tree stress check reproduced RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration in both lookup methods. get_note_ids() is also unlocked and does not promise a stable snapshot.

docs.title: In-memory structure
docs.text:
The index maps an entity type to normalized entity values and then to note IDs:

entity_type -> entity_value -> set[note_id]

Construction creates the 19 built-in type buckets. remove_note() preserves those buckets when their last value disappears. add_note() also accepts a new type key, so the key set can grow beyond the 19 built-in types during the instance lifetime. build() resets the index to the built-in buckets before it rebuilds the contents.

docs.title: Thread-safety contract
docs.text:
EntityIndexer uses one threading.RLock, stored as _flush_lock, for mutation, snapshot creation, loading, timer coordination, and dirty-state transitions.

Operation Locking in 2.8.0 Concurrent-use contract load() Holds _flush_lock while it reads and replaces known buckets Serialized with locked mutations on the same instance save() Copies the index under _flush_lock; writes the copy after releasing it Produces a stable point-in-time snapshot add_note() Holds _flush_lock for the complete mutation Serialized with load(), save() snapshots, remove_note(), and flushes remove_note() Holds _flush_lock for the complete mutation Serialized with load(), save() snapshots, add_note(), and flushes _schedule_flush() Holds _flush_lock while it inspects and creates the timer Starts at most one live timer per instance _flush_sync() Holds _flush_lock across dirty check, save(), and dirty clear Serializes a scheduled flush with mutations get_note_ids() Unlocked No stable-snapshot guarantee during mutation search_entities() Unlocked Unsafe during mutation; reproduced RuntimeError stats() Unlocked Unsafe during mutation; reproduced RuntimeError build() Does not lock the rebuild as one operation Run only with exclusive access to the instance

docs.title: Why the lock is reentrant
docs.text: _flush_sync() acquires _flush_lock and calls save(). save() acquires the same lock to create its snapshot. A non-reentrant threading.Lock would deadlock on that nested acquisition; threading.RLock lets the flush thread acquire the same lock again.

docs.title: What a saved snapshot means
docs.text:
save() copies every mapping while it holds _flush_lock. A concurrent add_note() or remove_note() cannot change the index during that copy. The method then releases the lock and writes the captured copy, so the file represents one complete point in time rather than every mutation that finishes before the disk write returns.

The background flush preserves later mutations: they set _dirty and schedule another flush when no live timer exists.

docs.title: Background flush lifecycle
docs.text:
add_note() and remove_note() mark the index dirty, then schedule a five-second daemon timer when no timer is alive. Mutations that arrive before that timer fires join the same batch. The timer calls _flush_sync(), which saves under the reentrant lock and clears _dirty after the save succeeds.

The constructor also registers _flush_sync() with atexit for a final flush on normal interpreter shutdown. A daemon timer does not keep a process alive.

build() cancels a live timer, saves synchronously, and clears _dirty before it returns. The rebuild itself lacks an operation-wide lock, so give build() exclusive access to the instance.

docs.title: File persistence contract
docs.text:
save() follows this sequence:

  1. Create a stable in-memory copy under _flush_lock.
  2. Create a temporary file in the target directory.
  3. Lock that temporary file with fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX).
  4. Write JSON, flush it, and call os.fsync() on the file.
  5. Unlock the temporary file and replace the target with os.replace().

On POSIX, the final replace gives readers atomic target-file visibility: they open the old complete file or the new complete file, not a partially written target. If serialization fails, save() deletes the temporary file and raises the exception.

docs.title: Cross-process limit
docs.text: Each writer creates and locks its own temporary file. Those locks do not serialize independent processes. When two processes save the same target path, each can complete its own snapshot and the last successful os.replace() wins. Use an external process lock when more than one process can write the same entity_index.json.

docs.title: EntityIndexer
docs.text:
Method Signature Result Constructor EntityIndexer(index_path: str \| None = None) Loads the default or supplied JSON index path load () -> bool True after a successful load; False when the path is absent or loading fails save () -> None Writes one atomic snapshot or raises the write error add_note (note_id: str, entities: dict[str, list[str]]) -> None Adds normalized values and schedules a flush remove_note (note_id: str) -> None Removes the note ID, prunes empty values, and schedules a flush get_note_ids (entity_type: str, entity_value: str) -> list[str] Returns matching note IDs or an empty list search_entities (query: str, limit: int = 10) -> dict[str, list[str]] Returns case-insensitive prefix matches, limited per type stats () -> dict Returns unique-entity and note-mapping counts per type build () -> dict Rebuilds from stored notes and returns count plus statistics

The following executed example shows the result shapes. It uses a temporary index and an explicit save():

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from zettelforge.entity_indexer import EntityIndexer

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    index_path = Path(directory) / "entity_index.json"
    indexer = EntityIndexer(index_path=str(index_path))
    indexer.add_note(
        "note-1",
        {"actor": ["APT28"], "tool": ["Cobalt Strike"]},
    )
    indexer.save()

    assert indexer.get_note_ids("actor", "apt28") == ["note-1"]
    assert indexer.search_entities("cobalt") == {
        "tool": ["cobalt strike"],
    }
    print(indexer.stats()["actor"])

Output:

{'unique_entities': 1, 'total_mappings': 1}

docs.title: Verification boundary
docs.text: The ZettelForge 2.8.0 release passed 35 focused entity-indexer and conversational- entity tests during this audit. A separate bounded stress check reproduced the two concurrent lookup failures described above. The official regression suite covers atomic save, temporary-file cleanup, built-in bucket preservation, and concurrent save-plus-add behavior; it does not assert concurrent-read safety.

docs.title: Governance controls
docs.text:
ZettelForge 2.8.0 validates memory writes and recall queries before they reach storage or retrieval. Use this reference to confirm the implemented content limit, prompt-injection guard, optional PII handling, recall timeout behavior, and write-time anomaly gate.

Prerequisites: Install ZettelForge with the Quickstart, then use the Configuration reference to locate your active config.yaml.

In progress: three configured controls do not fully enforce their intent

governance.enabled and governance.min_content_length exist in the configuration dataclass, but the ZettelForge 2.8.0 write path does not pass them into GovernanceValidator. Setting enabled: false does not disable the implemented checks, and min_content_length does not reject short or empty strings.

governance.limits.recall_timeout_seconds detects an overrun and changes the result to an empty list. The current executor waits for the retrieval worker to finish before returning control, so this setting is not a hard wall-clock latency cap.

docs.title: Direct write path
docs.text:
The default mm.remember(content) path applies controls in this order:

  1. Structural validation rejects values that are neither strings nor objects with a content attribute. The public remember() signature declares content as a string.
  2. Content length rejects content above governance.limits.max_content_length when the value is greater than zero.
  3. Prompt-injection detection rejects the first matching hostile pattern.
  4. PII handling runs when governance.pii.enabled is true and the optional analyzer is available.
  5. Note construction builds the memory note from the accepted or redacted content.
  6. Memory anomaly evaluation compares the note with recent same-domain reference notes.
  7. Storage and indexing write the note and then update the vector index.

Content-limit, prompt-injection, and blocking PII failures raise GovernanceViolationError before note construction. A flagged anomaly raises MemoryAnomalyError in block or quarantine mode. An unexpected anomaly evaluation error is logged and the write continues.

docs.title: Recall path
docs.text:
mm.recall(query) checks the query with the same prompt-injection guard before retrieval. A match raises PromptInjectionError immediately.

When recall_timeout_seconds is greater than zero, recall runs in a worker. An overrun records recall_timed_out and discards the worker result by returning an empty list after the worker finishes. A value of 0 runs retrieval without the timeout wrapper.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text: All keys live under the governance block in config.yaml.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: Key Default Environment variable Runtime state enabled true none Defined but not wired into the 2.8.0 validator or write path. min_content_length 1 none Defined but not enforced by the 2.8.0 validator.

docs.title: governance.limits
docs.text: Key Default Environment variable Runtime behavior max_content_length 52428800 ZETTELFORGE_LIMITS_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH Rejects remember() content when len(content) exceeds the value. 0 disables the check. The current exception text says “bytes,” but the implementation counts Python string characters. recall_timeout_seconds 30.0 ZETTELFORGE_LIMITS_RECALL_TIMEOUT Marks an overrun and returns [] after the retrieval worker finishes. 0 disables the wrapper.

docs.title: governance.pii
docs.text:
PII detection is disabled by default. It requires the pii optional extra, which installs Microsoft Presidio and spaCy support. If you enable PII handling without a usable analyzer, validation logs pii_validation_skipped and stores the original content.

Key Default Environment variable Runtime behavior enabled false ZETTELFORGE_PII_ENABLED Enables PII analysis before storage. action "log" ZETTELFORGE_PII_ACTION Selects log, redact, or block. redact_placeholder "[REDACTED]" none Replaces every selected PII span in redact mode. entities [] none Detects every supported type except the CTI allowlist. A non-empty list requests exactly those types. language "en" none Sets the Presidio language. nlp_model "en_core_web_sm" none Sets the spaCy model used by Presidio.

The detect-all CTI allowlist excludes IP_ADDRESS, URL, and DOMAIN_NAME because those values are common threat indicators. An explicit entities list is not filtered through that allowlist.

Action Result log Logs entity types and confidence scores without detected text, then stores the original content. redact Replaces detected spans with redact_placeholder, then stores the processed content. block Raises GovernanceViolationError at the validator boundary before storage.

docs.title: governance.memory_defense
docs.text:
The memory anomaly gate compares a candidate with recent same-domain notes before a direct write. The default audit mode logs a flagged decision and allows the write. block rejects the write. quarantine writes a JSONL forensic record and then rejects the write.

Key Default Environment variable Runtime behavior enabled true ZETTELFORGE_MEMORY_DEFENSE_ENABLED Enables anomaly evaluation. mode "audit" ZETTELFORGE_MEMORY_DEFENSE_MODE Selects audit, block, or quarantine. An unknown value falls back to audit. min_calibration_notes 50 ZETTELFORGE_MEMORY_DEFENSE_MIN_CALIBRATION Requires this many valid reference notes before scoring. max_reference_notes 50 none Caps valid reference notes used per evaluation. kappa 2.0 ZETTELFORGE_MEMORY_DEFENSE_KAPPA Multiplies calibration standard deviation in the threshold. lexical_weight 0.25 none Weights character n-gram Jensen-Shannon divergence. ngram_size 3 none Sets the character n-gram size. monitored_domains [] none Evaluates every domain when empty; otherwise evaluates listed domains only. quarantine_path "" none Resolves an empty value to <data_dir>/quarantine/memory_anomalies.jsonl. quarantine_raw_content true none Includes raw content in quarantine records. Set it to false when the record must omit content.

docs.title: Anomaly scoring
docs.text:
The embedding term is 0.5 × maximum cosine similarity + 0.5 × mean cosine similarity. The final score adds lexical_weight × lexical Jensen-Shannon divergence over character n-grams.

Calibration scores each reference note against the other reference notes. The threshold is calibration mean + kappa × calibration standard deviation. A candidate is flagged only when its score is greater than that threshold.

The gate returns without scoring in these cases:

Condition Action reason enabled=false allow disabled Domain not listed in monitored_domains allow domain_not_monitored Candidate embedding missing or all-zero audit candidate_embedding_unavailable Too few valid reference notes audit calibration_insufficient Leave-one-out calibration produces no scores audit calibration_unscorable

docs.title: Prompt-injection patterns
docs.text:
ZettelForge normalizes control characters and whitespace, then evaluates six deterministic regular-expression patterns in order. The guard returns the first matching code and raises PromptInjectionError.

Code Pattern intent instruction_override Ignore, disregard, forget, bypass, or override earlier instructions or rules. role_rewrite Replace the model role or activate admin, root, jailbreak, or developer-mode framing. secret_exfiltration Reveal, print, dump, show, exfiltrate, leak, or return hidden prompts, credentials, or secrets. tool_or_network_command Call, invoke, use, run, or execute a tool, shell, HTTP request, or webhook. prompt_boundary_marker Insert a begin/end marker for a system, developer, assistant, or tool prompt or message. memory_poisoning_intent Store content as a system, developer, or highest-priority instruction or memory.

remember() wraps this error as GovernanceViolationError. Recall and other direct guard call sites expose PromptInjectionError.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text: Exception Module When raised GovernanceViolationError zettelforge.governance_validator Structural validation, content length, prompt-injection, or PII validation rejects a write. PromptInjectionError zettelforge.prompt_injection_guard A direct prompt guard call finds one of the six pattern codes. PIIBlockedError zettelforge.pii_validator The raw PII validator finds PII in block mode; the governance boundary wraps it. MemoryAnomalyError zettelforge.memory_defense A candidate is flagged in block or quarantine mode. The exception carries its MemoryAnomalyDecision.

docs.title: Minimal hardening configuration
docs.text:
Enable PII redaction and switch the anomaly gate to block only after the store has at least min_calibration_notes clean same-domain references:

governance:
  limits:
    max_content_length: 1048576
    recall_timeout_seconds: 15.0
  pii:
    enabled: true
    action: redact
  memory_defense:
    enabled: true
    mode: block
    kappa: 2.0

Set the environment-backed subset with:

export ZETTELFORGE_PII_ENABLED=true
export ZETTELFORGE_PII_ACTION=redact
export ZETTELFORGE_MEMORY_DEFENSE_MODE=block
export ZETTELFORGE_LIMITS_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH=1048576

block mode does not reject a candidate before calibration exists. Until the gate has enough valid reference notes, it returns calibration_insufficient and allows the write.

docs.title: KG edge schema reference
docs.text:
Module: zettelforge.knowledge_graph

from zettelforge.knowledge_graph import KnowledgeGraph, get_knowledge_graph

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
ZettelForge maintains a knowledge graph of entities and typed relationships extracted from analyst notes and detection rules. The graph stores entity nodes and directed relationship edges with optional temporal indexing for time-based queries.

Prerequisites: Use ZettelForge v2.8.0 with Python 3.10 or newer. The direct KnowledgeGraph examples on this page use local JSONL files and do not require a graph service. If you use MemoryManager, read the Memory Manager API first.

Two storage paths exist in parallel:

  • SQLite (default). When you use MemoryManager with the default backend, KG writes go to the kg_nodes and kg_edges tables in zettelforge.db. This is the primary path for most deployments.
  • JSONL in-process. The KnowledgeGraph class (below) writes to kg_nodes.jsonl and kg_edges.jsonl in the data directory. It is used when you call get_knowledge_graph() directly or when the TypeDB extension is not installed and the backend is explicitly set to something other than SQLite.

The edge field names and relationship types are identical in both OSS paths. The SQLite edge table adds a note_id column (see below).

This page is the OSS ZettelForge schema reference. ThreatRecall.ai SaaS uses its own tenant-scoped PostgreSQL kg_nodes and kg_edges tables with tenant_id, TLP, confidence, and SaaS-specific node and edge columns. Do not treat the OSS DDL below as the SaaS database contract; use the Web API reference for SaaS integration behavior.

TypeDB is not part of the public ZettelForge package in this checkout. Direct get_knowledge_graph() access returns JSONL unless the process is configured with a compatible graph extension. Default MemoryManager writes stay on SQLite.

Thread safety: The public add_node() and add_edge() write paths use threading.RLock.

docs.title: Feature state
docs.text:
Core node and edge storage, SQLite DDL, JSONL node and edge writes, relationship labels, the functional OSINT relationships listed below, and the examples on this page were verified against ZettelForge v2.8.0 on August 18, 2026.

The direct JSONL temporal helper is in progress. In this run, one add_temporal_edge() call produced two identical get_changes_since() entries for the same change. The helper also stores timestamps verbatim and compares them as strings; it does not call _parse_timestamp() to validate or normalize them. Use consistently formatted ISO 8601 timestamps and deduplicate JSONL temporal results by (timestamp, from, relationship, to) before presenting them. The SQLite graph row shape remains verified.

docs.title: Node schema
docs.text: Nodes are created automatically when edges reference them. The entity_type field identifies the domain; the entity_value holds the canonical string.

docs.title: Node fields
docs.text: Field Type Description node_id str node_<12-hex> — internal primary key entity_type str Entity type string (see taxonomy below) entity_value str Canonical value, e.g. apt28, CVE-2024-3094 properties dict Application-specific metadata created_at str ISO 8601 updated_at str ISO 8601

docs.title: Entity type taxonomy
docs.text:
Entity types written by each subsystem. Strings are case-sensitive and written exactly as shown.

CTI domain (written by MemoryManager._update_knowledge_graph()):

entity_type Description note MemoryNote stored via remember() actor Threat actor via regex extraction threat_actor Threat actor via LLM NER intrusion_set Intrusion set (e.g. APT group) tool Malware or tool name cve Vulnerability identifier asset Target asset or sector campaign Campaign name attack_pattern MITRE ATT&CK technique (e.g. T1059) malware Malware family name person Person name (conversational domain) location Location (conversational domain) organization Organization name event Named event activity Activity name temporal Temporal reference extracted from text

Sigma and YARA domain (written by sigma/YARA ingest):

entity_type Description SigmaRule Sigma detection rule YaraRule YARA detection rule SigmaTag Raw Sigma tag string YaraTag Raw YARA tag string LogSource Sigma logsource facet AttackPattern MITRE ATT&CK technique resolved from tag Vulnerability CVE resolved from tag IntrusionSet MITRE ATT&CK group resolved from sigma tag Malware MITRE ATT&CK software resolved from sigma tag ThreatActor Named threat actor resolved from YARA metadata

OSINT domain (written by functional collectors):

entity_type Description DomainName Domain seed or discovered domain IPv4Address IPv4 address resolved from DNS, WHOIS, or BGP context IPv6Address IPv6 address resolved from DNS, WHOIS, or BGP context ASNumber Autonomous system number Netblock CIDR network block MXRecord Mail exchanger record NSRecord Name server record Port Network port discovered by the opt-in active scanner Organization Registrar, registrant, or owning organization EmailAddress Email seed or WHOIS registrant address Alias Username or handle used as an OSINT seed CryptoWallet Cryptocurrency wallet address Transaction Blockchain transaction SocialAccount Account found for an alias Breach Named breach associated with an email address

The OSINT module declares more ontology types than its functional collectors write. This reference lists only the OSINT nodes and relationships observed from v2.8.0 collectors and focused tests.

docs.title: SQLite DDL
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kg_nodes (
    node_id       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    entity_type   TEXT NOT NULL,
    entity_value  TEXT NOT NULL,
    properties    TEXT DEFAULT '{}',
    created_at    TEXT,
    updated_at    TEXT,
    UNIQUE(entity_type, entity_value)
);

docs.title: Edge schema
docs.text: Each edge is a directed relationship between two nodes.

docs.title: Edge fields
docs.text: Field Type Description edge_id str edge_<12-hex> — internal primary key from_node_id str Source node node_id to_node_id str Target node node_id relationship str Semantic relationship type (see below) edge_type str heuristic | causal | detection | osint (default: heuristic) properties dict Edge-specific metadata created_at str ISO 8601 updated_at str ISO 8601

docs.title: SQLite DDL
docs.text:
The SQLite path adds note_id, which links an edge back to the note that caused it. The unique constraint includes note_id, so the same entity pair can have the same relationship recorded from multiple notes.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kg_edges (
    edge_id       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    from_node_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
    to_node_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
    relationship  TEXT NOT NULL,
    edge_type     TEXT DEFAULT 'heuristic',
    note_id       TEXT DEFAULT '',
    properties    TEXT DEFAULT '{}',
    created_at    TEXT,
    updated_at    TEXT,
    UNIQUE(from_node_id, to_node_id, relationship, note_id)
);

The JSONL path deduplicates on (from_node_id, to_node_id, relationship) without note_id.

docs.title: Edge type taxonomy
docs.text:
The edge_type field records how the edge was created:

edge_type Description Source heuristic Co-occurrence or heuristic extraction (default) Entity co-occurrence during remember() causal LLM-extracted cause-and-effect triple Causal triple extraction in slow-path enrichment detection Detection rule relationship Sigma/YARA ingest osint Validated collector result OSINT collection executor

When add_edge() is called on an existing heuristic edge with a more specific edge_type, the type is promoted to the more specific value.

docs.title: CTI entity relationships
docs.text:
Created automatically during remember() with domain="cti".

Relationship From To Description MENTIONED_IN any entity note Entity appeared in a note USES_TOOL actor, threat_actor, intrusion_set tool Actor uses a specific tool EXPLOITS_CVE actor, threat_actor, intrusion_set, tool cve Entity exploits a vulnerability TARGETS_ASSET actor, threat_actor, intrusion_set, tool asset Entity targets an asset or sector CONDUCTS_CAMPAIGN actor, threat_actor, intrusion_set campaign Actor runs a campaign USES_TECHNIQUE actor, threat_actor, intrusion_set attack_pattern Actor uses an ATT&CK technique IMPLEMENTS malware attack_pattern Malware implements a technique

Conversational entity relationships (extracted when domain is not restricted to CTI):

Relationship From To Description AFFILIATED_WITH person organization Person affiliated with an org ATTENDED person event Person attended an event LOCATED_AT person location Person located at a place PARTICIPATES_IN person activity Person participates in an activity HELD_AT event location Event held at a location ORGANIZED_BY event organization Event organized by an org OCCURRED_ON event temporal Event at a temporal reference BASED_IN organization location Organization based in a location

Note versioning:

Relationship From To Description SUPERSEDES note note Newer note version supersedes the older one

docs.title: LLM causal relationships
docs.text:
Created by NoteConstructor.store_causal_edges() during slow-path enrichment. These edges have edge_type="causal". Extraction requires a configured LLM provider.

Relationship Description causes Subject is a direct cause of object enables Subject enables or facilitates object targets Subject targets object uses Subject uses object exploits Subject exploits object attributed_to Subject is attributed to object related_to Generic causal relationship

The relationship value is the lowercase string as validated against CAUSAL_RELATIONS (note_constructor.py:98). Node entity_type and entity_value for causal edges are free-form strings extracted by the LLM and are not constrained to the entity type taxonomy above.

docs.title: Detection rule relationships
docs.text:
Created during Sigma and YARA ingest.

Relationship From To Description applies_to SigmaRule LogSource Rule applies to a log source facet tagged_with SigmaRule, YaraRule SigmaTag, YaraTag Rule carries a tag detects SigmaRule, YaraRule AttackPattern Rule detects an ATT&CK technique references_cve SigmaRule, YaraRule Vulnerability Rule references a CVE attributed_to SigmaRule, YaraRule IntrusionSet, Malware, ThreatActor Rule attributed to a group or actor superseded_by SigmaRule SigmaRule Rule replaced by a newer version related_to SigmaRule SigmaRule Generic rule relationship

docs.title: OSINT relationships
docs.text:
Created by functional zettelforge.osint collectors through run_osint_collection(). Passive collectors write through the normal KG API. The port scanner writes only when you explicitly enable active scanning with ZETTELFORGE_OSINT_ACTIVE_SCAN=1.

Relationship From To Description resolves_to DomainName IPv4Address, IPv6Address DNS A or AAAA result ns_for DomainName NSRecord DNS NS record mx_for DomainName MXRecord DNS MX record owned_by DomainName, Netblock Organization WHOIS registrant or netblock owner associated_with IPv4Address, IPv6Address Netblock IP address belongs to a netblock part_of_as IPv4Address, IPv6Address, Netblock ASNumber IP address or netblock is announced by an autonomous system listens_on IPv4Address, IPv6Address Port Active scanner found an open port related_to DomainName DomainName Certificate transparency SAN domain association registered_by DomainName EmailAddress WHOIS data names a registrant email address has_account Alias SocialAccount Account discovery links a handle to a platform account appeared_in_breach EmailAddress Breach Breach lookup associates an email address with a named breach sent_transaction CryptoWallet Transaction Wallet appears as the transaction sender received_transaction CryptoWallet Transaction Wallet appears as the transaction recipient

The OSINT ontology also declares hosts, delegated_to, receives_mail_on, and controls_wallet. No v2.8.0 functional collector emitted those relationships during this audit, so treat them as declared vocabulary, not observed writes.

docs.title: Temporal relationships
docs.text:
For tracking entity state over time. Used with add_temporal_edge().

Relationship Description TEMPORAL_BEFORE State or event occurred before another TEMPORAL_AFTER State or event occurred after another SUPERSEDES New entity state supersedes an old one

Temporal edges are indexed automatically in _temporal_index and _entity_timeline on write.

docs.title: Legacy schema normalization
docs.text:
Edges written by pre-v2.5.1 deployments used different key names. _normalize_edge_schema() rewrites them on load:

Legacy key Canonical key source_id from_node_id target_id to_node_id relation_type relationship

Rules for rejected entries:

  • Entry missing edge_id: dropped.
  • Entry missing from_node_id, to_node_id, or relationship (and no recoverable legacy keys): dropped.
  • Malformed JSON line: skipped; total count logged at warning level as kg_edges_skipped_malformed.

This was a production hotfix (v2.5.1) for long-running deployments where pre-v2.5.x writers had written ~80k+ legacy entries alongside canonical-shape rows in kg_edges.jsonl.

docs.title: KnowledgeGraph class API
docs.text: Use KnowledgeGraph directly when you need in-process JSONL graph access, or call get_knowledge_graph() for the shared singleton.

docs.title: add_node()
docs.text:
def add_node(self, entity_type: str, entity_value: str, properties: dict | None = None) -> str:
    ...

Creates or updates a node. Returns node_id. If the node already exists, merges properties and refreshes updated_at.

docs.title: add_edge()
docs.text:
def add_edge(
    self,
    from_type: str,
    from_value: str,
    to_type: str,
    to_value: str,
    relationship: str,
    properties: dict | None = None,
) -> str:
    ...

Creates or updates a directed edge. Auto-creates both endpoint nodes. Deduplicates on (from_node_id, to_node_id, relationship). If a duplicate exists with edge_type="heuristic" and you pass a more specific edge_type in properties, it is promoted.

docs.title: get_node()
docs.text:
def get_node(self, entity_type: str, entity_value: str) -> dict | None:
    ...

Looks up a node by type and value. Returns None if not found.

docs.title: get_node_by_id()
docs.text:
def get_node_by_id(self, node_id: str) -> dict | None:
    ...

Looks up a node by its internal node_id.

docs.title: get_outgoing_edges()
docs.text:
def get_outgoing_edges(self, node_id: str) -> list[dict]:
    ...

Returns all outgoing edges for a node_id. Each dict contains at minimum edge_id, from_node_id, to_node_id, relationship, properties, created_at, updated_at.

docs.title: get_neighbors()
docs.text:
def get_neighbors(
    self, entity_type: str, entity_value: str, relationship: str | None = None
) -> list[dict]:
    ...

Returns adjacent nodes reachable via outgoing edges, with optional relationship filter. Each result contains node (the target node dict), relationship, and edge_properties.

docs.title: traverse()
docs.text:
def traverse(self, start_type: str, start_value: str, max_depth: int = 2) -> list[dict]:
    ...

Depth-first traversal up to max_depth. Returns a list of paths; each path is a list of step dicts with keys from_type, from_value, relationship, to_type, to_value.

docs.title: add_temporal_edge()
docs.text:
def add_temporal_edge(
    self,
    from_type: str,
    from_value: str,
    to_type: str,
    to_value: str,
    relationship: str,    # TEMPORAL_BEFORE | TEMPORAL_AFTER | SUPERSEDES
    timestamp: str,
    properties: dict | None = None,
) -> str:
    ...

Creates an edge and indexes it in _temporal_index (keyed by timestamp string) and _entity_timeline (keyed by "entity_type:entity_value").

docs.title: Timestamp handling
docs.text:
add_temporal_edge() stores the timestamp string you pass without validation. get_changes_since() filters and sorts those strings lexicographically. Use one fixed-width ISO 8601 representation, such as 2026-01-15T00:00:00Z, throughout a graph so string order matches chronological order.

The private _parse_timestamp() helper can parse the following formats, but the public temporal write and query methods do not call it in v2.8.0:

  • ISO 8601 (including Z suffix)
  • %Y-%m-%d
  • %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S
  • %d %b %Y (e.g. 15 Jan 2026)
  • %B %d, %Y (e.g. January 15, 2026)

docs.title: get_entity_timeline()
docs.text:
def get_entity_timeline(self, entity_type: str, entity_value: str) -> list[dict]:
    ...

Returns the chronological state history for an entity. Each entry: {"edge": dict, "timestamp": str, "to_entity": "type:value"}.

docs.title: get_changes_since()
docs.text:
def get_changes_since(self, timestamp: str) -> list[dict]:
    ...

Returns temporal entity changes whose stored timestamp string is lexicographically greater than or equal to timestamp. Results are sorted by that string. Each entry: {"timestamp": str, "from": "type:value", "relationship": str, "to": "type:value"}.

docs.title: get_latest_state()
docs.text:
def get_latest_state(self, entity_type: str, entity_value: str) -> dict | None:
    ...

Returns the most recent temporal edge entry for an entity, or None if no temporal data exists.

docs.title: Causal edge queries
docs.text: Causal edges (edge_type: "causal") represent LLM-extracted cause-and-effect triples. Two dedicated methods traverse them.

docs.title: get_causal_edges()
docs.text:
def get_causal_edges(
    self, entity_type: str, entity_value: str,
    max_depth: int = 3, max_visited: int = 50,
) -> list[dict]:
    ...

BFS over outgoing causal edges — traces forward from cause to effects. Useful for "what does this actor or event lead to?" queries.

docs.title: get_incoming_causal()
docs.text:
def get_incoming_causal(
    self, entity_type: str, entity_value: str,
    max_depth: int = 3, max_visited: int = 50,
) -> list[dict]:
    ...

BFS over incoming causal edges — traces back to root causes. Useful for "why did this happen?" queries.

docs.title: Global singleton
docs.text:
from zettelforge.knowledge_graph import KnowledgeGraph


def get_knowledge_graph() -> KnowledgeGraph:
    ...

Returns the process-global KnowledgeGraph instance for direct graph access. Checks ZETTELFORGE_BACKEND (default: sqlite):

  • If ZETTELFORGE_BACKEND=typedb and a compatible TypeDB graph extension is importable, it tries that extension.
  • Otherwise, it returns the JSONL KnowledgeGraph instance.

When you use MemoryManager with the default SQLite backend, KG writes go directly to the SQLite tables via self.store.add_kg_edge(), not through get_knowledge_graph(). Call get_knowledge_graph() for direct graph access independent of the memory manager.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
from zettelforge.knowledge_graph import KnowledgeGraph

kg = KnowledgeGraph()

# Add nodes and an edge
kg.add_node("actor", "apt28")
kg.add_node("tool", "cobalt strike")
edge_id = kg.add_edge("actor", "apt28", "tool", "cobalt strike", "USES_TOOL")

# Query neighbors
neighbors = kg.get_neighbors("actor", "apt28")
for n in neighbors:
    print(f"{n['relationship']} -> {n['node']['entity_type']}:{n['node']['entity_value']}")
# Output: USES_TOOL -> tool:cobalt strike

# Traverse up to depth 2
paths = kg.traverse("actor", "apt28", max_depth=2)
for path in paths:
    print(" -> ".join(
        f"{p['from_type']}:{p['from_value']} [{p['relationship']}] {p['to_type']}:{p['to_value']}"
        for p in path
    ))

from zettelforge.knowledge_graph import KnowledgeGraph

kg = KnowledgeGraph()

# Temporal edge: record that an event preceded another
kg.add_temporal_edge(
    from_type="actor", from_value="apt28",
    to_type="campaign", to_value="nato-phishing-2026-q1",
    relationship="TEMPORAL_BEFORE",
    timestamp="2026-01-15",
)

# What changed since the start of Q1?
changes = kg.get_changes_since("2026-01-01")
for c in changes:
    print(f"[{c['timestamp']}] {c['from']} {c['relationship']} {c['to']}")

# Causal chain: forward (cause → effects)
causes = kg.get_causal_edges("actor", "apt28", max_depth=3)

# Causal chain: backward (root cause analysis)
root_causes = kg.get_incoming_causal("campaign", "nato-phishing-2026-q1", max_depth=3)

docs.title: MCP Protocol Reference
docs.text: The ZettelForge MCP server implements the Model Context Protocol specification (protocol version 2024-11-05) over stdio transport using JSON-RPC 2.0.

docs.title: Protocol overview
docs.text: Property Value Transport stdio (stdin for requests, stdout for responses) Protocol JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP version 2024-11-05 Server name zettelforge Tools available 7 Version reported 2.7.0 Lazy initialization MemoryManager is instantiated on first tool call, not on import

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
The MCP lifecycle has three phases:

client                          server
  |                               |
  |--- initialize --------------->|  Phase 1: Initialization
  |<-- initialize result ---------|
  |--- notifications/initialized->|  (no response)
  |                               |
  |--- tools/list --------------->|  Phase 2: Tool discovery
  |<-- tools list ----------------|
  |                               |
  |--- tools/call --------------->|  Phase 3: Tool execution
  |<-- tool result ---------------|
  |                               |
  |--- tools/call --------------->|
  |<-- tool result ---------------|

docs.title: Lazy singleton contract
docs.text:
Importing zettelforge.mcp (or zettelforge.mcp.server) does not instantiate MemoryManager. The initialize and tools/list methods work without touching the backend. MemoryManager is created on the first tools/call that reaches handle_tool_call(). Tool introspection is therefore side-effect-free.

from zettelforge.mcp import TOOLS, run_stdio

# TOOLS is a static list — no backend started
assert len(TOOLS) == 7

# run_stdio reads stdin, processes requests, writes stdout
run_stdio()

docs.title: TLP access control
docs.text:
Every tool that reads from or writes to memory enforces TLP (Traffic Light Protocol) access control. The actor parameter identifies the caller:

  • No actor (default): unauthenticated calls are capped at TLP:GREEN. Notes marked TLP:AMBER, TLP:AMBER+STRICT, or TLP:RED are filtered from results.
  • Authenticated actor: a caller matching the configured single-user identity receives results up to TLP:RED.
  • TLP override: callers may request results above their sharing ceiling by providing a non-empty tlp_override_reason. The override is audited to a JSONL log.

The actor value is resolved from these argument keys in order: actor, caller, identity, user.

Default TLP for new notes is TLP:CLEAR.

docs.title: zettelforge_remember
docs.text:
Store threat intelligence in memory. Extracts entities (actors, CVEs, tools, campaigns) and populates the knowledge graph. With evolve=true (default), uses an LLM to compare against existing notes and decides whether to add, update, or supersede.

Input schema:

Property Type Required Default Description content string yes — Threat intelligence text to store domain string no "cti" Domain: cti, incident, general tlp string no "TLP:CLEAR" TLP marking for the note actor string no — Caller identity for audit attribution source string no "mcp" Source reference string evolve boolean no true Enable memory evolution (LLM-based dedup/merge)

TLP enum values: TLP:CLEAR, TLP:WHITE, TLP:GREEN, TLP:AMBER, TLP:AMBER+STRICT, TLP:RED (and short aliases without the TLP: prefix).

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "zettelforge_remember",
    "arguments": {
      "content": "APT28 used CVE-2024-3094 against NATO networks.",
      "domain": "cti",
      "source": "report-2026-001",
      "tlp": "TLP:AMBER",
      "evolve": true
    }
  }
}

Response fields:

Field Type Description note_id string or null ID of the created/updated note, or null on error status string "created", "updated", "corrected", "noop" entities string[] Up to 10 extracted entity values tlp string TLP marking applied to the stored note

docs.title: zettelforge_recall
docs.text:
Search memory using blended vector + graph retrieval. Returns ranked results with entities, confidence scores, tier metadata, and TLP labels.

Input schema:

Property Type Required Default Description query string yes — Natural language search query k integer no 10 Maximum number of results domain string no — Optional domain filter actor string no — Caller identity; unauthenticated calls are capped at TLP:GREEN tlp_override_reason string no — Audited reason to return content above the caller's sharing ceiling

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "zettelforge_recall",
    "arguments": {
      "query": "What tools does APT28 use?",
      "k": 10,
      "domain": "cti"
    }
  }
}

Response fields:

Field Type Description results object[] Ranked search results results[].id string Note ID results[].content string First 500 characters of note content, wrapped in BEGIN_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT … END_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT markers results[].content_is_untrusted boolean Always true; content has passed prompt-injection screening but must be treated as untrusted results[].context string Clean semantic context string (content without the UNTRUSTED wrapper, safe to display) results[].entities string[] Up to 10 extracted entities results[].tier string Epistemic tier: "A" (authoritative), "B" (operational, default), "C" (support) results[].tlp string TLP marking of the note results[].confidence number Confidence score (0.0 to 1.0) count integer Number of results returned latency_ms integer Query latency in milliseconds tlp_share_max string Effective TLP ceiling applied to this response tlp_override boolean Whether a TLP override was applied

docs.title: zettelforge_synthesize
docs.text:
Generate a synthesized answer from ZettelForge memories using RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation). Requires a configured LLM provider; without one, returns a well-formed response with answer: "No specific answer found" and confidence: 0.0.

Input schema:

Property Type Required Default Description query string yes — Question to answer from memory format string no "direct_answer" Output format (see below) actor string no — Caller identity; unauthenticated calls are capped at TLP:GREEN tlp_override_reason string no — Audited reason to use sources above the caller's sharing ceiling

Format values:

Value Description direct_answer Concise answer with source attribution. Works in OSS with a configured LLM. synthesized_brief Structured intelligence brief. Available via ThreatRecall.ai SaaS; falls back to direct_answer in OSS. timeline_analysis Chronological event sequence. Available via ThreatRecall.ai SaaS; falls back to direct_answer in OSS. relationship_map Entity relationship summary. Available via ThreatRecall.ai SaaS; falls back to direct_answer in OSS.

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "zettelforge_synthesize",
    "arguments": {
      "query": "What is APT28's targeting pattern in 2026?",
      "format": "direct_answer"
    }
  }
}

Response fields:

Field Type Description synthesis object The generated answer synthesis.answer string The synthesized answer text; "No specific answer found" when no LLM is configured synthesis.confidence number Answer confidence (0.0 to 1.0); 0.0 when no LLM is configured synthesis.sources string[] Note IDs cited by the LLM in its answer; empty when no LLM is configured sources_count integer Number of memory notes retrieved as candidates (non-zero even without LLM) sources object[] Retrieved candidate notes (see fields below) sources[].note_id string Note ID sources[].relevance_score number Retrieval relevance score (0.0 to 1.0) sources[].quote string First characters of note content, wrapped in BEGIN_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT … END_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT sources[].tier string Epistemic tier: "A" (authoritative), "B" (operational), "C" (support) sources[].tlp string TLP marking of the source note tlp_max string Highest TLP level seen among sources tlp_share_max string Effective TLP ceiling applied tlp_override boolean Whether a TLP override was applied

docs.title: zettelforge_entity
docs.text:
Fast entity lookup by type. Uses an O(1) index for direct entity-to-note mapping.

Input schema:

Property Type Required Default Description type string yes — Entity type advertised by the MCP schema value string yes — Entity value (e.g. "apt28", "CVE-2024-3094") k integer no 5 Maximum results actor string no — Caller identity; unauthenticated calls are capped at TLP:GREEN tlp_override_reason string no — Audited reason to return content above the caller's sharing ceiling

Advertised MCP enum values:

Type Indexing notes actor Generic actor references that are not normalized to a named intrusion set cve CVE identifiers (e.g. "CVE-2024-3094") tool Malware and attack tooling names campaign Named campaigns person Individual names location Geographic locations

The backend entity index can contain additional types such as intrusion_set, attack_pattern, domain, url, ipv4, md5, sha1, sha256, email, and organization. In ZettelForge 2.7.0, tools/list does not advertise those values for zettelforge_entity, so they are invalid against the advertised tool schema and schema-validating MCP clients reject them before the server receives the call.

The entity indexer (entity_indexer.py) assigns APT-numbered groups (e.g. APT28, APT29) to intrusion_set, not actor. Use zettelforge_graph for direct graph traversal from intrusion_set values, and pass the normalized lowercase form as value (e.g. "apt28", not "APT28").

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 4,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "zettelforge_entity",
    "arguments": {
      "type": "cve",
      "value": "CVE-2024-3094",
      "k": 5
    }
  }
}

Response fields:

Field Type Description results object[] Notes referencing this entity results[].id string Note ID results[].content string First 300 characters of note content, wrapped in BEGIN_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT … END_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT results[].content_is_untrusted boolean Always true; treat as untrusted results[].tier string Epistemic tier: "A" (authoritative), "B" (operational), "C" (support) results[].tlp string TLP marking of the note count integer Number of results tlp_share_max string Effective TLP ceiling applied tlp_override boolean Whether a TLP override was applied

docs.title: zettelforge_graph
docs.text:
Traverse the STIX 2.1 knowledge graph starting from a given entity. Shows relationships such as uses, targets, attributed-to. Returns up to 20 paths.

Input schema:

Property Type Required Default Description type string yes — Starting entity type value string yes — Starting entity value max_depth integer no 2 Maximum traversal depth

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 5,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "zettelforge_graph",
    "arguments": {
      "type": "intrusion_set",
      "value": "apt28",
      "max_depth": 2
    }
  }
}

Response fields:

Field Type Description paths object[][] Up to 20 graph traversal paths paths[][].from string Source entity value paths[][].rel string Relationship type paths[][].to string Target entity value count integer Number of paths found

docs.title: zettelforge_stats
docs.text:
Return memory system statistics: version, total note count, retrieval count, and entity index breakdown.

Input schema: No parameters.

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 6,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "zettelforge_stats",
    "arguments": {}
  }
}

Response fields:

Field Type Description version string ZettelForge version string (e.g. "2.7.0") total_notes integer Total number of stored notes retrievals integer Cumulative retrieval count since last restart entity_index object Entity type counts; each key maps to {unique_entities, total_mappings}

The entity_index keys reflect what has been ingested. A populated deployment includes: cve, intrusion_set, actor, tool, campaign, attack_pattern, ipv4, domain, url, md5, sha1, sha256, email, person, location, organization, event, activity, temporal. Types with no data still appear with zero counts.

docs.title: zettelforge_sync
docs.text:
Expose the native OpenCTI sync placeholder. This tool is present in the tool list for all installations, but the current ZettelForge OSS release returns an error response instead of syncing. Native OpenCTI pull/push sync is in progress. ThreatRecall.ai currently supports manual STIX 2.1 import and export workflows for OpenCTI, not automatic OpenCTI sync from this MCP tool.

Input schema:

Property Type Required Default Description limit integer no 20 Maximum objects to pull per STIX type

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 7,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "zettelforge_sync",
    "arguments": {
      "limit": 20
    }
  }
}

Response (OSS installation):

The tool returns a content-level error response in the current OSS release. This is isError: false at the JSON-RPC level -- the tool call succeeds, but the content text reports that native sync is unavailable.

Response (ThreatRecall.ai SaaS):

Native MCP sync response shape is not verified for ThreatRecall.ai SaaS in this docs run. Treat automatic OpenCTI sync from this tool as in progress and use the manual STIX exchange path in Configure OpenCTI.

docs.title: initialize
docs.text:
The client sends initialize as the first message to negotiate protocol version and discover server capabilities.

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 0,
  "method": "initialize",
  "params": {
    "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
    "capabilities": {},
    "clientInfo": {
      "name": "my-client",
      "version": "1.0.0"
    }
  }
}

Response:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 0,
  "result": {
    "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
    "capabilities": {
      "tools": {
        "listChanged": false
      }
    },
    "serverInfo": {
      "name": "zettelforge",
      "version": "2.7.0"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: notifications/initialized
docs.text:
Sent by the client after receiving the initialize response. The server does not send a response; it silently skips this message.

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "notifications/initialized"
}

docs.title: tools/list
docs.text:
Return the full list of available tools with their input schemas.

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/list"
}

Response: Returns a tools array containing all 7 tool definitions, each with name, description, and inputSchema.

docs.title: tools/call
docs.text:
Execute a named tool with the provided arguments.

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "zettelforge_recall",
    "arguments": {
      "query": "APT28",
      "k": 5
    }
  }
}

Response (success):

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "{ ... }"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Response (tool error):

Tool errors do not use JSON-RPC error codes. They are returned as successful JSON-RPC responses with isError: true in the result payload and the error message inside the text content:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "{\"error\": \"Unknown tool: zettelforge_nonexistent\"}"
      }
    ],
    "isError": true
  }
}

docs.title: JSON-RPC standard error codes
docs.text: Code Meaning When it occurs -32700 Parse error Invalid JSON in request -32600 Invalid request Request object is malformed -32601 Method not found Unknown method (not initialize, tools/list, tools/call, or notifications/initialized) -32602 Invalid params Tool arguments fail schema validation (handled by the MCP client; the server does not validate schemas) -32603 Internal error Unhandled exception in the tool handler

docs.title: Method-not-found response example
docs.text:
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 9,
  "error": {
    "code": -32601,
    "message": "Unknown method: does/not/exist"
  }
}

docs.title: Tool-level errors
docs.text: Scenario Error message Unknown tool name "Unknown tool: {name}" OpenCTI sync not available Content-level error from the current OSS runtime; native sync is in progress OpenCTI sync failure Connector or runtime exception from a future native sync implementation Backend connection failure Connection error from MemoryManager

docs.title: Backward compatibility
docs.text:
Tool names prefixed with threatrecall_ (for example threatrecall_stats, threatrecall_remember) are transparently rewritten to zettelforge_* before dispatch:

if name.startswith("threatrecall_"):
    name = name.replace("threatrecall_", "zettelforge_", 1)

Existing agent workflows and configurations that reference the old naming continue to work without changes.

docs.title: Memory Manager API reference
docs.text: MemoryManager is the main Python interface to ZettelForge memory. Use it to store notes, retrieve context, inspect relationships, and synthesize answers. This page gives you the public signatures and the behavior observed in ZettelForge 2.8.0.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Install ZettelForge 2.8.0 on Python 3.10 or later. Review the configuration reference before you enable LLM-backed enrichment or synthesis.

The signatures below come from the official v2.8.0 source tag. The runtime examples were exercised against a fresh, isolated SQLite and LanceDB store.

docs.title: Get an instance
docs.text:
from zettelforge import MemoryManager

mm = MemoryManager()

MemoryManager(jsonl_path: str | None = None, lance_path: str | None = None)
  • jsonl_path defaults to None. This compatibility path selects the data directory through its parent and is passed to the vector-store adapter.
  • lance_path defaults to None and overrides the LanceDB index path.

Call get_memory_manager() when you want the process-wide singleton instead of an explicit instance. Construction initializes SQLite, LanceDB access, and the background enrichment worker.

Background enrichment dispatch is enabled by default. Set ZETTELFORGE_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED=false before import when you need a deterministic offline write path. Disabling dispatch does not disable regex entity extraction or direct storage.

docs.title: remember
docs.text:
remember(
    content: str,
    source_type: str = "conversation",
    source_ref: str = "",
    domain: str = "general",
    evolve: bool = False,
    sync: bool = False,
) -> tuple[MemoryNote, str]

Creates one memory note. The direct path constructs an embedding, writes the note, updates entity mappings and graph edges, and returns (note, status). status is "created", "updated", "corrected", or "noop".

When background enrichment is enabled, sync=False queues causal extraction and sync=True runs it inline. Set evolve=True to run fact extraction and the ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / NOOP decision path before direct storage.

note, status = mm.remember(
    "APT28 used Mimikatz against the target network.",
    source_type="threat_report",
    source_ref="sample-report",
    domain="cti",
)

The ZettelForge 2.8.0 public signature does not accept per-call TLP arguments.

docs.title: remember_chunked
docs.text:
remember_chunked(
    content: str,
    source_type: str = "conversation",
    source_ref: str = "",
    domain: str = "general",
    chunk_size: int = 800,
    sync: bool = False,
) -> list[MemoryNote]

Splits long content on sentence boundaries and stores each chunk through remember(). Content at or below chunk_size becomes one note. Longer input gets source references such as report#c0, report#c1, and report#c2.

docs.title: remember_with_extraction
docs.text:
remember_with_extraction(
    content: str,
    source_type: str = "conversation",
    source_ref: str = "",
    domain: str = "general",
    context: str = "",
    min_importance: int = 3,
    max_facts: int = 5,
) -> list[tuple[MemoryNote | None, str]]

Uses an LLM to extract scored facts, then compares each retained fact with existing notes and applies an operation. Facts below min_importance are discarded, and max_facts limits extraction. Each result is (note, status); the status is "added", "updated", "corrected", or "noop".

The method rejects explicit prompt-injection patterns in content and context with PromptInjectionError before it calls the model.

docs.title: remember_report
docs.text:
remember_report(
    content: str,
    source_url: str = "",
    published_date: str = "",
    domain: str = "cti",
    min_importance: int = 3,
    max_facts: int = 10,
    chunk_size: int = 3000,
) -> list[tuple[MemoryNote | None, str]]

Chunks a report and sends each chunk through remember_with_extraction(). When present, published_date is added to the extraction context as Published: <date>. The source reference for each chunk uses the form <source_url>:chunk:<index>.

LLM prerequisite

remember_with_extraction() and remember_report() require a reachable, configured LLM for fact output. With a deliberately unreachable provider, both returned an empty list. remember(evolve=True) fell through to direct storage and returned "created" when extraction produced no facts.

docs.title: recall
docs.text:
recall(
    query: str,
    domain: str | None = None,
    k: int = 10,
    include_links: bool = True,
    exclude_superseded: bool = True,
    include_expired: bool = False,
    caller: str | None = None,
    actor: str | None = None,
) -> list[MemoryNote]

Retrieves notes with blended vector, entity, and graph search. The intent classifier selects retrieval weights. When cross-encoder reranking is enabled, ZettelForge reranks only the configured head of the candidate list and keeps the tail in blended order.

caller records telemetry attribution. actor is its compatibility alias; caller wins when both are supplied. Superseded and expired notes are excluded by default.

If governance.limits.recall_timeout_seconds is greater than zero, a timeout logs a warning and returns an empty list. Explicit prompt-injection patterns in query raise PromptInjectionError before retrieval.

The ZettelForge 2.8.0 public signature has no per-call TLP filter or override.

docs.title: Direct entity lookups
docs.text:
recall_entity(entity_type: str, entity_value: str, k: int = 5) -> list[MemoryNote]
recall_cve(cve_id: str, k: int = 5) -> list[MemoryNote]
recall_actor(actor_name: str, k: int = 5) -> list[MemoryNote]
recall_technique(technique_id: str, k: int = 25) -> list[MemoryNote]
recall_tool(tool_name: str, k: int = 5) -> list[MemoryNote]

These methods bypass the blended scoring pipeline and read entity mappings directly.

  • recall_cve() normalizes the identifier to uppercase.
  • recall_actor() checks actor, threat_actor, and intrusion_set, then removes duplicate notes.
  • recall_technique() checks the attack_pattern type.
  • recall_tool() normalizes the tool name to lowercase.

The built-in entity index tracks activity, actor, attack_pattern, campaign, cve, domain, email, event, intrusion_set, ipv4, location, md5, organization, person, sha1, sha256, temporal, tool, and url. External loaders can add other type strings because recall_entity() does not validate the type.

Direct lookup resolves only mappings already in the index. Alias enrichment depends on the LLM enrichment path.

docs.title: get_context
docs.text:
get_context(
    query: str,
    domain: str | None = None,
    k: int = 10,
    token_budget: int = 4000,
) -> str

Returns formatted memory context for an agent prompt. Explicit prompt-injection patterns in query raise PromptInjectionError.

docs.title: get_stats
docs.text:
get_stats() -> dict

Returns the current counters plus store and entity-index totals. ZettelForge 2.8.0 returns these top-level keys:

  • notes_created, retrievals, entity_index_hits, and consolidations_triggered
  • llm_ner_success, llm_ner_failure, llm_ner_no_new, llm_ner_total_new_entities, and llm_ner_total_duration_ms
  • total_notes and entity_index

These are process counters, not durable historical metrics.

docs.title: flush
docs.text:
flush(timeout: float | None = None) -> bool

Waits for queued and in-flight enrichment jobs. It returns True when all jobs finish. It returns False when a supplied timeout expires first.

docs.title: evolve_note
docs.text:
evolve_note(note_id: str, sync: bool = False) -> dict | None

Runs neighbor evolution for an existing note. With sync=True, it returns the evolution report. With sync=False, it queues the job and returns None. A missing note_id also returns None and logs a warning.

docs.title: mark_note_superseded
docs.text:
mark_note_superseded(note_id: str, superseded_by_id: str) -> bool

Links the old and new notes, removes the old note from entity mappings, and writes a SUPERSEDES temporal edge. It returns False when either identifier does not resolve.

docs.title: snapshot
docs.text:
snapshot() -> str

Creates a storage snapshot under the configured data directory.

In progress in ZettelForge 2.8.0

The observed SQLite snapshot was created as snapshots/zettelforge_<timestamp>.db, but snapshot() returned a snapshots/notes_<timestamp>.jsonl path that did not exist. Inspect the snapshots directory for the .db file instead of trusting the returned path. The 2.8.0 signature accepts no arguments.

docs.title: ingest_relationship
docs.text:
ingest_relationship(
    from_type: str,
    from_value: str,
    to_type: str,
    to_value: str,
    relationship: str,
    properties: dict | None = None,
) -> None

Writes a relationship without creating a note. The SQLite edge identity uses the source node, target node, relationship, and note identifier. Repeating the same direct relationship produced one matching edge in the isolated store.

docs.title: provenance_chain
docs.text:
provenance_chain(
    entity_type: str,
    entity_value: str,
    max_depth: int = 3,
    direction: str = "forward",
) -> list[dict]

Returns causal steps from the canonical entity. direction="forward" follows outgoing edges; direction="backward" follows incoming edges. Any other value raises ValueError.

Each step has this shape:

{
    "from_entity": ...,
    "relationship": ...,
    "to_entity": ...,
    "edge_type": ...,
    "note_id": ...,
}

docs.title: get_entity_relationships
docs.text:
get_entity_relationships(entity_type: str, entity_value: str) -> list[dict]

Alias-resolves the entity value and returns its direct graph neighbors. Each observed result contained node, relationship, edge_properties, and note_id.

docs.title: traverse_graph
docs.text:
traverse_graph(
    start_type: str,
    start_value: str,
    max_depth: int = 2,
) -> list[dict]

Traverses outward from the canonical start entity. ZettelForge clamps requests above depth 2 to depth 2 and logs the clamp.

Return annotation mismatch

The source annotation says list[dict], but the observed value was a list of paths. Each path was a list of step dictionaries with from_type, from_value, relationship, to_type, and to_value. Treat the runtime value as list[list[dict]] until the implementation or annotation is fixed.

docs.title: synthesize
docs.text:
synthesize(
    query: str,
    format: str = "direct_answer",
    k: int = 10,
    tier_filter: list[str] | None = None,
    caller: str | None = None,
    actor: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]

Retrieves notes and asks the configured LLM for an answer. k limits the retrieved notes. A missing tier_filter becomes ['A', 'B', 'C']. caller records telemetry attribution, and actor is its compatibility alias.

The verified format is "direct_answer". Requests for "synthesized_brief", "timeline_analysis", or "relationship_map" are logged and fall back to "direct_answer". No current ThreatRecall.ai public synthesis surface was verified for the other formats, so they remain in progress rather than documented as available SaaS behavior.

Explicit prompt-injection patterns in query or retrieved context raise PromptInjectionError. The public signature has no per-call TLP filter or override.

The returned dictionary has this shape:

{
    "query": ...,
    "format": "direct_answer",
    "synthesis": {"answer": ..., "confidence": ..., "sources": [...]},
    "metadata": {
        "query_id": ...,
        "model_used": ...,
        "tokens_used": ...,
        "latency_ms": ...,
        "confidence_threshold": ...,
        "sources_count": ...,
        "tier_filter": ...,
    },
    "sources": [
        {
            "note_id": ...,
            "relevance_score": ...,
            "quote": ...,
            "tier": ...,
        }
    ],
}

With a deliberately unreachable provider, the method still returned the full wrapper, a direct_answer fallback with confidence 0.0, and the retrieved source records. It preserved the wrapper shape, but validation returned False because confidence was below the configured threshold.

docs.title: validate_synthesis
docs.text:
validate_synthesis(response: dict) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]

Returns (is_valid, errors) after checking a synthesis response.

docs.title: check_synthesis_quality
docs.text:
check_synthesis_quality(response: dict) -> dict

Returns a score from 0 to 1, a quality label, and component scores. The no-provider fallback scored 0.48 and NEEDS_WORK in the isolated run.

docs.title: Feature state
docs.text:
This page remains in_progress for three precise reasons:

  1. A real LLM response was not observed, so extracted facts, alias enrichment, causal extraction, and generated synthesis content remain unverified.
  2. snapshot() creates a SQLite file but returns a nonexistent JSONL path.
  3. traverse_graph() returns nested path lists while its public annotation says list[dict].

All public signatures, direct write and recall paths, entity lookup, graph ingest and traversal, prompt-injection rejection, no-provider fallbacks, synthesis validation, statistics, and flush() were verified on 2026-08-16 against the official ZettelForge 2.8.0 source tag.

docs.title: Module inventory
docs.text:
Use this page to find the ZettelForge module that owns a behavior before you read, extend, or debug the code. This inventory covers the immutable ZettelForge v2.8.0 release tag; paths are relative to the repository root.

Prerequisites: You have the ZettelForge v2.8.0 source tree. For installation and first use, start with Quickstart.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
Metric Verified value Python files under src/zettelforge/ 107 Package directories with __init__.py 17 Public exports in zettelforge.__all__ 29 Root-level Python files under web/ 3 JavaScript files under web/ui/ 17 Most-imported package module zettelforge.log — 48 dependents

The 107 package files divide into 42 top-level modules and 65 modules in the detection, integration, LLM-provider, MCP, OSINT, script, Sigma, and YARA subtrees. The web files are outside that package count.

The seven files under src/zettelforge/llm_providers/ isolate provider-specific behavior behind one contract.
