docs.title: Operator scripts
docs.text:
The release contains four Python modules under src/zettelforge/scripts/ and no __init__.py in that directory.

File Responsibility compact_lance.py Runs one-shot LanceDB compaction. human_eval_sampler.py Samples items for human evaluation. telemetry_aggregator.py Aggregates daily telemetry records. telemetry_dashboard.py Runs the Streamlit telemetry dashboard.

docs.title: Web layer
docs.text:
The web application lives outside src/zettelforge/ and is not included in the 107-module package count.

Root Python file Responsibility web/app.py FastAPI application with 21 /api/* route decorators and two HTML route decorators. web/auth.py API-key validation and loopback access rules. web/mcp_server.py MCP adapter for web deployment.

The 17 JavaScript files under web/ui/ contain one bootstrap file, two library files, six components, and eight views. The UI uses the checked-in stylesheets web/static/css/design_tokens.css and web/ui/colors_and_type.css; it has no generated JavaScript bundle in the release tree.

docs.title: Dependency map
docs.text:
Use these seams to choose where a change belongs:

memory_manager
├── backend_factory → storage_backend → sqlite_backend
├── vector_retriever → vector_memory, entity_indexer
├── graph_retriever → knowledge_graph
├── blended_retriever → vector_retriever, graph_retriever
├── synthesis_generator → llm_client
├── note_constructor → entity_indexer, note_schema
├── fact_extractor → llm_client, json_parse
├── memory_updater → note_schema
├── governance_validator → pii_validator, prompt_injection_guard, memory_defense
├── enrichment_ledger → deferred enrichment job records
└── log → structured events across 48 dependent modules

Start in memory_manager.py when you trace a user-visible memory operation. Move down one seam to change a storage, retrieval, synthesis, validation, or enrichment implementation without widening the change across unrelated layers.

docs.title: Retrieval policies
docs.text:
Use this reference to trace how ZettelForge 2.8.0 ranks notes when you call MemoryManager.recall(). The read path classifies your query, retrieves vector and graph candidates, blends those two scored signals, adds intent-specific candidates, reranks a bounded head, applies result filters, and returns at most k notes.

Prerequisite: Read the Memory Manager API for the public recall() signature. Read the Configuration reference before you change retrieval settings.

Retrieval controls are in progress

ZettelForge loads retrieval.default_k, retrieval.similarity_threshold, retrieval.entity_boost, and retrieval.max_graph_depth, but MemoryManager.recall() does not read those four values in v2.8.0. Pass k to recall() directly. The direct read path uses the VectorRetriever constructor defaults and passes graph depth 2 directly.

The LanceDB branch also does not apply VectorRetriever.similarity_threshold. Treat threshold configuration as in progress. The run-238 verification of the high-fanout entity boundary also fails, so do not treat retrieval.entity_max_fanout as a guaranteed cutoff until that defect is resolved.

docs.title: Read-path order
docs.text:
MemoryManager.recall() executes these stages in order:

  1. Classify the query and load its policy dictionary.
  2. Extract and resolve query entities, then apply the high-fanout filter.
  3. Retrieve scored vector candidates.
  4. For a temporal query, move candidates containing recognized query dates to the head when dateparser is installed.
  5. Traverse the active store's knowledge graph to depth 2.
  6. Normalize and blend vector and graph scores.
  7. Fall back to the vector list when blending returns fewer notes than vector retrieval produced.
  8. For a causal query, add notes reached through forward and incoming causal edges.
  9. Add up to three entity-index notes per resolved query entity.
  10. Rerank a bounded head when reranking is enabled.
  11. Filter superseded and expired notes according to the recall() arguments.
  12. Truncate the final list to k.

The policy dictionary does not control every stage. Only its vector and graph fields enter normalized score fusion. Entity, temporal, causal, rerank, and final-limit behavior use separate logic.

docs.title: Intent classification
docs.text: Module: zettelforge.intent_classifier

docs.title: Intent values
docs.text:
Value Meaning Example factual Direct fact or entity lookup What CVE was used in the SolarWinds attack? temporal Time or change query What changed since May 2024? relational Relationship or graph query Who uses Cobalt Strike? causal Cause-and-effect query Why did the attacker pivot? exploratory Broad context query and classifier fallback Tell me about APT28 unknown Enum and policy value available to callers The built-in classifier does not return this value as its no-match fallback.

With the default IntentClassifier(use_llm_fallback=False), a query with no accepted keyword result returns exploratory with confidence 0.3 and method default.

docs.title: Keywords
docs.text:
The classifier lowercases the query and counts substring matches.

Intent Keywords factual cve-, cve, vulnerability, exploit, threat, what is, what was, who is, name, identify temporal when, timeline, since, before, after, changed, history, previously, earlier, latest, recent relational who uses, who targets, who conducts, what tools does, what malware does, what technique, what cve does, used by, attributed to, related to, connected to, associated with, linked to, uses tool, between, relationship, connection, link, which actor, which group, which apt, what does causal why, because, caused by, enables, leads to, results in, due to, reason for exploratory tell me about, explain, describe, overview, information on, details about, context, summarize, what do we know, brief

docs.title: Decision rules
docs.text:
Condition Result Best score is at least 2 Return the best intent; confidence is min(1.0, score / 4); method is keyword. Best score is 1 and no other intent has a positive score Return the best intent; confidence is 0.6; method is keyword_unambiguous. Neither rule accepts the result and LLM fallback is enabled Call the LLM classifier with max_tokens=20 and temperature=0.1. A recognized response has confidence 0.8 and method llm. LLM classification fails or returns an unrecognized value Return exploratory; confidence is 0.5; method is llm_fallback. Neither keyword rule accepts the result and LLM fallback is disabled Return exploratory; confidence is 0.3; method is default.

get_intent_classifier() creates its global classifier with LLM fallback disabled.

docs.title: Policy dictionary
docs.text:
IntentClassifier.get_traversal_policy() returns these values:

Intent vector entity_index graph temporal top_k factual 0.3 0.7 0.2 0.0 3 temporal 0.2 0.1 0.2 0.5 5 relational 0.2 0.2 0.5 0.1 10 causal 0.1 0.1 0.6 0.2 10 exploratory 0.5 0.2 0.2 0.1 10 unknown 0.4 0.2 0.2 0.2 5

The four weights total 1.2 for factual and 1.0 for every other row. ZettelForge does not normalize the whole policy dictionary.

docs.title: Runtime use
docs.text: Field Runtime effect in MemoryManager.recall() vector Multiplies the normalized vector score during BlendedRetriever.blend(). graph Multiplies the normalized graph score during BlendedRetriever.blend(). entity_index Not consumed. Entity augmentation uses a fixed k=3 per resolved entity. temporal Not consumed. Temporal handling reorders date-matching vector tuples without changing their scores. top_k Not consumed. The k argument passed to recall() controls retrieval and the final limit.

docs.title: Vector retrieval
docs.text: Module: zettelforge.vector_retriever

docs.title: Constructor defaults
docs.text:
Parameter Default Effect similarity_threshold 0.15 Filters the in-memory branch after boosts. The LanceDB branch does not apply it. entity_boost 2.5 Multiplies a score once per overlapping resolved entity. exact_match_boost 1.0 Multiplies once for each resolved query entity whose text appears in the note content. The default leaves the score unchanged. regenerate_invalid_embeddings True Regenerates invalid note vectors in the in-memory branch. memory_store None Creates a MemoryStore when you do not pass one. note_lookup None Uses the retriever's store unless you provide a cross-backend lookup.

retrieve() defaults to domain=None, k=10, include_links=True, use_lancedb=True, and return_scores=False.

docs.title: Return values
docs.text:
return_scores Return value False list[MemoryNote] True list[tuple[MemoryNote, float]]

MemoryManager.recall() requests scores because the blend stage requires them.

docs.title: In-memory scoring
docs.text:
The in-memory branch computes cosine similarity. A zero-norm input produces 0.0.

For each candidate, the branch applies these multipliers before thresholding:

  • Entity overlap: entity_boost ** overlap_count.
  • Exact text matches: one exact_match_boost multiplier for each resolved query entity found in the note content.

The branch keeps a note when its boosted score is at least similarity_threshold, sorts retained notes by score, and keeps the first k before link expansion.

The branch treats an embedding as invalid when it is missing, has a length other than 768, contains only zeros, or has variance below 0.001. With regeneration enabled, it calls get_embedding() on the first 1,000 content characters. It skips a note when the resulting vector remains invalid.

The default embedding configuration uses provider fastembed, model nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5-Q, and 768 dimensions.

docs.title: LanceDB scoring
docs.text:
When LanceDB is available and enabled, the retriever searches each selected table, requests up to k * 2 rows, and calculates a score as 1.0 - row["_distance"]. It sorts across tables, keeps the first k, applies entity and exact-match boosts, and then expands links.

This branch does not apply similarity_threshold and does not run the in-memory embedding validation routine. If LanceDB raises an exception or returns no usable result, retrieve() runs the in-memory branch.

docs.title: Link expansion
docs.text: With include_links=True, each directly related note receives parent_score * 0.5. The retriever de-duplicates linked note IDs and returns at most k * 2 vector-stage results.

docs.title: Graph retrieval
docs.text:
Module: zettelforge.graph_retriever

GraphRetriever.retrieve_note_ids() accepts query_entities: dict[str, list[str]] and defaults max_depth to 2. MemoryManager.recall() wraps its active storage backend in StoreGraphSource, which reads the same per-store knowledge graph populated by the write path.

The graph source supplies get_node(), get_node_by_id(), and get_outgoing_edges(). Breadth-first search starts at each resolved entity and scores every reached note as 1 / (1 + hops).

Hops Score 0 1.000 1 0.500 2 0.333

When more than one path reaches a note, the result keeps the shortest path. retrieve_note_ids() sorts ScoredResult values by descending score. Each result contains note_id, score, hops, and path.

docs.title: Normalized score fusion
docs.text:
Module: zettelforge.blended_retriever

BlendedRetriever.blend() normalizes vector and graph scores independently with (score - minimum) / (maximum - minimum). When every score in one signal is equal, it assigns 0.5 to every item in that signal.

It then calculates contributions as follows:

  • Vector contribution: normalized_vector_score * policy["vector"].
  • Graph contribution: normalized_graph_score * policy["graph"].
  • A note present in both signals receives the sum of both contributions.

The method sorts by the combined score and returns at most its k argument. It does not read entity_index, temporal, or top_k from the policy dictionary.

docs.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion alternative
docs.text: blend_rrf() is an available alternative, but MemoryManager.recall() calls blend() in v2.8.0. blend_rrf() defaults rrf_k to 60 and adds 1 / (rrf_k + rank) for every signal containing the note.

docs.title: Post-blend augmentation and reranking
docs.text:
The direct recall path performs additional work outside BlendedRetriever:

  • A causal intent traverses outgoing and incoming causal edges with max_depth=3 and max_visited=50, then adds note endpoints and source-note references.
  • Entity augmentation calls recall_entity(..., k=3) for every retained resolved query entity and de-duplicates note IDs.
  • Reranking processes only the first retrieval.rerank_max_candidates notes and the first retrieval.rerank_doc_chars characters of each note. The tail keeps its pre-rerank order.
  • A reranker load or scoring failure logs a warning and preserves the original order.

docs.title: Configuration status
docs.text: Key Default v2.8.0 direct-recall status retrieval.default_k 10 Loaded but not read; recall() defaults its own k to 10. retrieval.similarity_threshold 0.25 Loaded but not passed to VectorRetriever; its constructor defaults to 0.15, and LanceDB does not enforce either value. retrieval.entity_boost 2.5 Loaded but not passed to VectorRetriever; its constructor independently defaults to 2.5. retrieval.max_graph_depth 2 Loaded but not read; recall() passes 2 directly. retrieval.rerank_enabled true Read before reranking. retrieval.rerank_max_candidates 8 Bounds the reranked head. retrieval.rerank_doc_chars 256 Bounds candidate text sent to the reranker. retrieval.rerank_model Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 Selects the TextCrossEncoder model. retrieval.rerank_threads 8 Sets ONNX threads; 0 delegates to the runtime default. retrieval.entity_max_fanout 25 Supplies the high-fanout filter threshold; run-238 behavior verification fails and remains in progress.

docs.title: Sigma schema reference
docs.text:
Use this page to look up the ZettelForge Sigma parser, schema dispatch, entity mapping, ingest API, and command-line interface. The reference covers ZettelForge 2.8.0, released under the MIT license.

Modules: zettelforge.sigma, zettelforge.sigma.parser, zettelforge.sigma.entities, zettelforge.sigma.tags, zettelforge.sigma.ingest

In progress

Parsing, validation, entity mapping, persistence, and dry-run ingestion work in ZettelForge 2.8.0. Three mappings remain incomplete: filter bodies do not populate SigmaRule.detection_body, tlp.* tags do not populate SigmaRule.tlp, and sigma_format_version remains unset. See Current limitations.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: You need ZettelForge 2.8.0 and Python 3.10 or later. Use Configure Sigma ingestion for a task-oriented import procedure. Read Detection rules schema for the shared Sigma and YARA model.

docs.title: Public exports
docs.text:
zettelforge.sigma exports these names:

Name Kind Purpose SigmaRule dataclass Sigma-specific DetectionRule subtype SigmaParseError exception Reports YAML, file, and size errors SigmaValidationError exception Reports JSON Schema failures parse_yaml function Parses and validates YAML text parse_file function Reads, parses, and validates one file validate function Validates an existing rule dictionary from_rule_dict function Builds a SigmaRule and relation dictionaries without schema validation rule_to_entities alias Points to the same function as from_rule_dict resolve_sigma_tag function Resolves supported tag namespaces to typed entities ingest_rule function Persists one rule and its graph relations ingest_rules_dir function Walks and ingests a rule directory

docs.title: Processing layers
docs.text: Layer Module Responsibility Schema sigma.parser / sigma.schemas Load YAML and validate it against a vendored schema Entity sigma.entities / sigma.tags Map a validated dictionary to SigmaRule and relation dictionaries Ingest sigma.ingest Store the rule as a memory note and write knowledge-graph edges

docs.title: Vendored schemas
docs.text:
ZettelForge packages three SigmaHQ JSON schemas in src/zettelforge/sigma/schemas/. The parser loads them through importlib.resources, caches each loaded schema in _SCHEMA_CACHE, and requires no separate schema download.

File Schema title Required top-level fields Selected when sigma-detection-rule-schema.json Sigma rule specification V2.0.0 (2024-08-08) title, logsource, detection Neither correlation nor filter is present sigma-correlation-rules-schema.json Sigma Meta rule specification V2.1.0 (2025-07-25) title, correlation correlation is present sigma-filters-schema.json Sigma Global Filter specification V2.0.0 (2024-08-08) title, logsource, filter filter is present and correlation is absent

All three schemas declare JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Dispatch checks correlation first, then filter, then falls back to the detection schema. A dictionary containing both keys therefore selects the correlation schema.

docs.title: Top-level properties
docs.text: Property Type Required Description title string, max 256 yes Brief detection title id UUID string no Globally unique rule identifier name string, max 256 no Name used by correlation rule references related array of objects no Relationships to other rules taxonomy string, max 256 no Taxonomy identifier status enum string no Rule lifecycle state description string, max 65,535 no Detailed description references array of strings no External references author string no Rule author date date string no Creation date modified date string no Last modification date tags array of strings no Namespaced tags level enum string no Severity level logsource object yes Product, service, category, and definition fields detection object yes Selections plus required condition field falsepositives array of strings no Known false-positive scenarios fields array of strings no Output field names license string no License for the rule content, separate from the ZettelForge software license scope array no Scope values defined by the vendored Sigma schema

docs.title: status values
docs.text: Value Meaning stable Used in multiple environments for a long period without obvious false positives test Used on a limited set of test systems without obvious false positives experimental New and not tested outside lab environments deprecated Replaced by or covered by another rule linked through related unsupported Not usable in its current form

docs.title: level values
docs.text: Value Meaning informational Enrichment-only match that does not trigger a case or alert low Notable event that rarely represents an incident on its own medium Relevant event that needs regular manual review high Relevant event that triggers an internal alert and prompt review critical Incident-level event with near-certain significance

docs.title: logsource properties
docs.text: Property Type Description product string Product such as windows service string Product subset such as security or sshd category string Product group such as process_creation definition string Free-text source definition

docs.title: related[].type values
docs.text:
Value ZettelForge relation obsolete superseded_by derived related_to merged related_to renamed related_to similar related_to

Each related item requires id and type. Only obsolete produces superseded_by; every other supported value produces related_to.

docs.title: Correlation schema
docs.text:
The correlation schema requires title and correlation. The correlation object requires type, rules, and timespan.

Property Type Required Description correlation.type enum string yes Correlation calculation correlation.rules array of strings yes Referenced rule names or UUIDs correlation.timespan string, max 10 yes Lowercase number-plus-unit window such as 15m or 1h correlation.group-by array of strings conditional Fields that define separate event scopes correlation.condition object conditional Count comparison and, for value calculations, the target field correlation.aliases object no Field-name aliases applied to referenced rules

Supported correlation.type values are:

  • event_count
  • temporal
  • temporal_ordered
  • value_count
  • value_sum
  • value_avg
  • value_percentile

The schema also accepts optional correlation metadata such as id, status, description, author, references, date, modified, taxonomy, falsepositives, level, and generate.

docs.title: Filter schema
docs.text:
The filter schema requires title, logsource, and filter. The filter object requires all three fields below.

Property Type Description filter.rules array of strings Rule names that receive the filter filter.selection array or object Filter values or field/value pairs filter.condition string Relationship between the filter selections

The filter schema also accepts id, description, date, modified, and taxonomy.

docs.title: parse_yaml
docs.text:
Signature: parse_yaml(text: str) -> dict[str, Any]

parse_yaml loads YAML with yaml.safe_load, converts YAML date and datetime objects back to ISO-8601 strings, selects a schema, and validates the result. It returns the validated dictionary.

It raises:

  • SigmaParseError for invalid YAML or a top-level value that is not a mapping.
  • SigmaValidationError when the selected JSON Schema rejects the mapping.

docs.title: parse_file
docs.text:
Signature: parse_file(path: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]

parse_file reads one UTF-8 rule file and delegates to parse_yaml. It includes the path in parse and validation errors.

The parser enforces MAX_RULE_FILE_BYTES = 1_048_576 and raises SigmaParseError before YAML parsing when a file exceeds the limit. It also raises SigmaParseError when it cannot stat or read the path.

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
Signature: validate(rule: dict[str, Any]) -> ValidationResult

validate returns a ValidationResult instead of raising. The result contains:

Field Type Meaning valid bool True when the selected schema accepts the dictionary errors list[str] One path-prefixed message per validation failure

bool(result) returns result.valid. A dictionary with no title or logsource and with level: catastrophic returns these errors:

  • <root>: 'title' is a required property
  • <root>: 'logsource' is a required property
  • level: 'catastrophic' is not valid under any of the given schemas

docs.title: Error types
docs.text:
SigmaParseError and SigmaValidationError both extend ValueError.

Exception Raised for SigmaParseError Invalid YAML, non-mapping YAML, file stat/read failure, or an oversized file SigmaValidationError A parsed mapping that fails the selected JSON Schema

docs.title: DetectionRule
docs.text:
SigmaRule extends zettelforge.detection.base.DetectionRule.

Field Type Description rule_id str Upstream UUID or deterministic content-hash identifier title str Rule title source_format str sigma for Sigma rules content_sha256 str SHA-256 of the canonical, key-sorted YAML form description str \| None Rule description author str \| None Rule author date str \| None Creation date modified str \| None Modification date references list[str] External references tags list[str] Raw rule tags level str \| None Rule severity status str \| None Rule lifecycle state tlp str \| None Inherited TLP field; not populated by Sigma mapping in 2.8.0 license str \| None Rule-content license source_repo str \| None Upstream repository source_path str \| None Path inside the upstream repository extra dict[str, Any] Extension values

docs.title: SigmaRule
docs.text:
Field Type Default or behavior logsource_product str \| None Copied from logsource.product logsource_service str \| None Copied from logsource.service logsource_category str \| None Copied from logsource.category rule_level str \| None Raw level value rule_status str \| None Raw status value sigma_format_version str \| None Remains None in 2.8.0 detection_body str \| None YAML for detection or correlation; remains None for filters rule_type str detection, correlation, or filter fields list[str] Copied from fields, default [] falsepositives list[str] Copied from falsepositives, default []

When a rule has no id, ZettelForge sets rule_id to sigma_ plus the first 16 characters of the canonical content hash. The same rule content therefore produces the same fallback identifier.

docs.title: Entity conversion
docs.text:
Signature: from_rule_dict(rule_dict: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[SigmaRule, list[dict[str, Any]]]

rule_to_entities is the same function object as from_rule_dict. The function returns a populated SigmaRule plus a list of relation dictionaries. It does not validate its input; pass dictionaries through validate, parse_yaml, or parse_file first.

Each relation dictionary contains:

Key Value from_type SigmaRule from_value Source rule identifier rel ZettelForge relation name to_type Target entity type to_value Target entity value properties Optional relation metadata

docs.title: Emitted relations
docs.text:
Relation Target type Emitted when applies_to LogSource A product, service, or category logsource facet exists tagged_with SigmaTag A non-empty raw tag exists detects AttackPattern An attack.t* technique or sub-technique tag resolves references_cve Vulnerability A cve.* tag resolves attributed_to IntrusionSet An attack.g* group tag resolves attributed_to Malware An attack.s* software tag resolves superseded_by SigmaRule related[].type is obsolete related_to SigmaRule related[].type is another supported value

Logsource targets use facet:value, such as product:windows. ZettelForge always keeps a supported or unsupported tag as tagged_with; it adds a typed edge only when resolve_sigma_tag returns a target.

docs.title: Tag resolution
docs.text:
Signature: resolve_sigma_tag(tag: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None

Input Return value attack.t1059 ('AttackPattern', 'T1059') attack.t1059.001 ('AttackPattern', 'T1059.001') attack.g0007 ('IntrusionSet', 'G0007') attack.s0154 ('Malware', 'S0154') cve.2021-44228 ('Vulnerability', 'CVE-2021-44228') cve.2024.3094 ('Vulnerability', 'CVE-2024-3094') tlp.amber None detection.emerging None attack.initial-access None

CVE resolution accepts a dot or hyphen between the year and identifier and returns the canonical hyphenated value.

docs.title: ingest_rule
docs.text:
Signature: ingest_rule(rule, mm, *, domain='detection', source_ref=None, sync=True) -> tuple[note, relations]

Parameter Accepted value Default Behavior rule dictionary, YAML string, path string, or Path required Strings and paths are parsed and validated; dictionaries are used as-is mm MemoryManager-compatible object required Receives the note and knowledge-graph edges domain string detection Stored note domain source_ref string or None None Overrides the generated source reference sync boolean True Controls inline enrichment in MemoryManager.remember

The generated source reference is sigma:<rule_id>:<first-12-content-hash-characters>. If the store already contains that reference, the function returns the existing note and newly computed relations without persisting duplicates.

For a new rule, the function stores the YAML and a one-line summary as source_type='sigma_rule', then attempts to persist every relation. It raises ValueError when mm is None and propagates parser and validation errors from string and path inputs. Dictionary input bypasses schema validation.

docs.title: ingest_rules_dir
docs.text:
Signature: ingest_rules_dir(path, mm, *, glob='**/*.yml', domain='detection', bulk=False, flush_timeout=None) -> tuple[int, int]

The function returns (ingested, skipped). It raises FileNotFoundError when the root path does not exist. It matches both .yml and .yaml, logs per-file failures, increments skipped, and continues the walk.

When bulk=True, it calls each ingest_rule with sync=False and calls mm.flush(timeout=flush_timeout) once after the walk.

docs.title: Directory security controls
docs.text: Control Behavior File size parse_file rejects files larger than 1,048,576 bytes YAML loading yaml.safe_load prevents Python object construction Symlinks ingest_rules_dir skips symlinked files Root containment ingest_rules_dir skips resolved paths outside the requested root

docs.title: Knowledge-graph edge metadata
docs.text:
Before persistence, ingest_rule adds these properties unless the relation already supplies them:

Property Value Purpose edge_type detection Distinguishes detection edges from causal and heuristic edges source sigma_ingest Records ingest provenance

If one edge write raises an exception, ZettelForge logs sigma_edge_persist_failed and continues with the next relation.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The verified dry-run invocation against the v2.8.0 release fixture is:

python3 -m zettelforge.sigma.ingest --dry-run tests/fixtures/sigma/tagged_example.yml
Argument Default Description path required One .yml or .yaml file, or a directory --dry-run off Parses, validates, and maps without persistence --domain detection Memory domain for persisted notes --glob **/*.yml Directory glob; ZettelForge also checks the corresponding .yaml glob

A successful dry run writes:

OK  tests/fixtures/sigma/tagged_example.yml  id=7e3d88a2-bfaa-4f52-9e0b-2bbbdd0d4ea1  type=detection  tags=5  edges=11

Dry-run summary: 1/1 parsed, 0 failed.

ZettelForge 2.8.0 also exposes python3 -m zettelforge.sigma.cli. The ingest module invocation emits a non-fatal runpy warning on stderr because zettelforge.sigma.__init__ imports ingest before Python executes it as a module. The command still exits successfully; use the cli module to avoid that warning.

The CLI does not invoke the LLM rule explainer in 2.8.0.

docs.title: Quick reference example
docs.text:
This self-contained example parses a rule and inspects the entity relations without writing data:

from zettelforge.sigma import from_rule_dict, parse_yaml

yaml_text = """title: Command shell start
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image: cmd.exe
  condition: selection
tags:
  - attack.t1059.003
"""

rule_dict = parse_yaml(yaml_text)
entity, relations = from_rule_dict(rule_dict)
print(entity.rule_id, entity.rule_type)
print([(edge["rel"], edge["to_value"]) for edge in relations])

Output:

sigma_158aaf05e376149d detection
[('applies_to', 'product:windows'), ('applies_to', 'category:process_creation'), ('tagged_with', 'attack.t1059.003'), ('detects', 'T1059.003')]

docs.title: Current limitations
docs.text:
These ZettelForge 2.8.0 behaviors are in progress:

  • from_rule_dict validates filter rules and sets rule_type='filter', but it leaves detection_body=None instead of preserving the filter object.
  • tlp.* tags remain available through tags and tagged_with relations, but they do not populate the inherited tlp field.
  • sigma_format_version remains None for parsed detection, correlation, and filter rules.
  • from_rule_dict and dictionary input to ingest_rule bypass schema validation; validate dictionaries before calling either API.
  • The CLI parses, validates, maps, and persists rules, but it does not run the LLM rule explainer.

docs.title: STIX-aligned extraction and graph reference
docs.text: ZettelForge turns common CTI indicators and names into lowercase entity labels, then connects co-occurring entities in its local knowledge graph. Use this reference when you call an entity-recall method, inspect note metadata, or write a relationship directly.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• ZettelForge 2.8.0.
  • A MemoryManager instance when you use the recall or relationship methods.
  • A working LLM provider only when you need the conversational enrichment labels marked in progress below.

docs.title: Scope and naming
docs.text:
This page covers the ZettelForge open-source extraction index, note metadata, and the SQLite knowledge-graph path used by MemoryManager. It does not describe the hosted ThreatRecall.ai graph schema.

ZettelForge 2.8.0 has two related vocabularies. Keep their spelling separate:

  • The extraction index and MemoryManager use lowercase labels such as intrusion_set and uppercase graph relationships such as USES_TOOL.
  • The typed ontology validator uses PascalCase entities such as IntrusionSet and lowercase relationships such as uses_tool. It is a separate validation surface; do not pass its PascalCase names to the recall methods on this page.

docs.title: Extraction-index entity labels
docs.text: remember() runs the deterministic regex extractor before it writes entity mappings. Regex matches are lowercased, and spaces become hyphens. Match order is not stable because the extractor deduplicates with sets.

docs.title: CTI labels
docs.text: Label Example output Deterministic match cve cve-2024-3094 CVE- + four digits + at least four digits intrusion_set apt28, unc4990, ta505, fin7 APT, UNC, TA, FIN, or TEMP designation plus digits actor lazarus, sandworm, volt-typhoon One of the three built-in actor names tool cobalt-strike, metasploit, mimikatz, bloodhound, dropbear, empire, covenant One of the seven built-in tool names campaign operation-aurora operation followed by one word attack_pattern t1059, t1059.001 ATT&CK technique or sub-technique identifier

docs.title: Observable labels
docs.text:
Label Match ipv4 IPv4 address with each octet constrained to 0–255 domain Domain name with one of the suffixes registered in the extractor url Text beginning with http:// or https:// up to a delimiter md5 32 hexadecimal characters sha1 40 hexadecimal characters sha256 64 hexadecimal characters email Address-shaped text with a dotted suffix

The hash extractor rejects candidates that appear in assignment, Git commit, or fenced-code contexts. The URL regex does not strip terminal periods or commas; surround a URL with a delimiter or normalize the captured value before you use it as an IOC.

docs.title: Conversational labels
docs.text:
Label Deterministic path LLM enrichment path person A name of 3–16 letters at the start of a Name: dialogue line, minus the built-in stop list Broader person names location One of 43 built-in city or place names Broader locations organization None Named organizations event None Named events activity None Described activities temporal None Time expressions

Conversational LLM enrichment is in progress

No Ollama service was listening on 127.0.0.1:11434 during this run, so the LLM enrichment path was not verified. When generation fails, the extractor catches the error and returns empty lists for all six conversational labels. The deterministic person and location matches above were executed.

docs.title: Entity recall methods
docs.text:
Method ZettelForge 2.8.0 signature Lookup behavior recall_entity (entity_type: str, entity_value: str, k: int = 5) -> list[MemoryNote] Looks up one lowercase extraction-index label. It lowercases the value. recall_actor (actor_name: str, k: int = 5) -> list[MemoryNote] Searches actor, threat_actor, then intrusion_set, and removes duplicate notes. recall_technique (technique_id: str, k: int = 25) -> list[MemoryNote] Searches attack_pattern; the wrapper uppercases the input before the shared lookup lowercases it.

recall_entity() does not validate entity_type. An unknown label returns no mapped notes unless a caller has written mappings under that label.

docs.title: Note metadata fields
docs.text:
Every MemoryNote has a metadata object. These are the STIX-adjacent fields and related confidence fields in ZettelForge 2.8.0.

Field Type Default Meaning stix_confidence int -1 STIX confidence from 0–100; -1 means unset. The model does not enforce the range. tier str "B" Epistemic tier. A is authoritative, B operational, and C support. The model does not restrict other strings. tlp str "" Stored TLP text. ZettelForge 2.8.0 does not normalize or validate this field in Metadata. confidence float 1.0 Internal confidence. increment_evolution() caps it at 0.95. vuln VulnerabilityMeta | None None Structured vulnerability data attached by an import or sync path.

docs.title: VulnerabilityMeta
docs.text:
Field Type Default cvss_v3_score float | None None cvss_v3_vector str | None None epss_score float | None None epss_percentile float | None None cisa_kev bool False

The model describes the numeric ranges in comments but does not enforce bounds at construction time.

docs.title: Built-in SQLite graph relationships
docs.text:
remember() creates a note node, MENTIONED_IN edges, and heuristic edges for co-occurring entities. Heuristic edges store first_observed and the note's internal confidence as properties.

Relationship From To Writer MENTIONED_IN Any extracted entity note remember() USES_TOOL actor, threat_actor, intrusion_set tool remember() EXPLOITS_CVE Actor label or tool cve remember() TARGETS_ASSET Actor label or tool asset remember() when another path supplies asset entities CONDUCTS_CAMPAIGN Actor label campaign remember() USES_TECHNIQUE Actor label attack_pattern remember() IMPLEMENTS malware attack_pattern remember() when another path supplies malware entities AFFILIATED_WITH person organization LLM entity enrichment ATTENDED person event LLM entity enrichment LOCATED_AT person location LLM entity enrichment PARTICIPATES_IN person activity LLM entity enrichment HELD_AT event location LLM entity enrichment ORGANIZED_BY event organization LLM entity enrichment OCCURRED_ON event temporal LLM entity enrichment BASED_IN organization location LLM entity enrichment SUPERSEDES New note Old note mark_note_superseded()

The regex extractor does not emit asset or malware. Their rows activate only when an import, sync, or enrichment path supplies those entity lists. The eight conversational relationships remain in progress because this run did not exercise LLM enrichment.

docs.title: ingest_relationship()
docs.text:
The method accepts source and target labels, a relationship string, and optional properties. It returns None. The method does not validate the labels against the typed ontology.

mm.ingest_relationship(
    from_type="actor",
    from_value="apt28",
    to_type="tool",
    to_value="mimikatz",
    relationship="USES_TOOL",
    properties={"confidence": 0.9},
)

The SQLite edge key is the source node, target node, and relationship. Repeating the call updates the existing edge properties instead of adding another edge. The method also writes the same edge to the legacy JSONL knowledge graph for backward compatibility.

docs.title: Typed CTI ontology vocabulary
docs.text:
The separate OntologyValidator exposes these core CTI names in 2.8.0:

  • Entity types: IntrusionSet, ThreatActor, Vulnerability, Malware, Campaign, Incident, and AttackPattern.
  • Relationship types: attributed_to, uses, uses_technique, uses_tool, exploits, implements, and targets.

Use this PascalCase/snake_case vocabulary only with the ontology validation surface. Use the lowercase/uppercase vocabulary in the earlier tables with MemoryManager.

docs.title: Terminology reference
docs.text:
This page is the single source of truth for product names, API identifiers, and entity type vocabulary used across ZettelForge documentation. When in doubt, prefer the forms listed here over informal variations.

Prerequisites: None. This page describes the public names and identifiers in ZettelForge 2.8.0 and the canonical name of the hosted ThreatRecall.ai product.

docs.title: Product names
docs.text:
Term Use Avoid ZettelForge The open-source CTI memory engine. Always one word, always capitalized. "Zettelforge", "zettelforge", "ZF" in prose ThreatRecall.ai The hosted SaaS product. One word, capital T and R, with lowercase ai after the dot. "ThreatRecall", "Threat Recall", "threatrecall" in prose ZettelForge OSS Acceptable short form when distinguishing from SaaS in the same sentence. "ZettelForge open source" after the first mention

ThreatRecall.ai is the commercial hosted product. ZettelForge is the MIT-licensed open-source engine. They share a core but are distinct products; do not use the names interchangeably.

docs.title: Core API classes
docs.text: Term Description MemoryManager The main Python class. PascalCase, two words joined. MemoryNote The data model for a stored memory. PascalCase. get_memory_manager() Process-wide singleton factory function. snake_case.

docs.title: API methods
docs.text:
Use the exact method names from source; do not shorten or paraphrase them in code examples or inline code spans.

Method Description remember() Store one note. remember_chunked() Split and store a long text as multiple notes. remember_with_extraction() Two-phase LLM extraction into notes. remember_report() Ingest a news or threat report with chunking and extraction. recall() Retrieve notes by blended vector and graph retrieval. recall_actor() Entity-index lookup by actor name. recall_cve() Entity-index lookup by CVE ID. recall_tool() Entity-index lookup by tool name. recall_technique() Entity-index lookup by ATT&CK technique ID. recall_entity() Entity-index lookup by type and value. synthesize() Retrieval-augmented answer generation. ingest_relationship() Write a knowledge graph edge directly. traverse_graph() Walk relationship paths outward from an entity. get_entity_relationships() Return direct knowledge graph neighbors of an entity. get_context() Return a formatted context string for agent prompts. flush() Block until background enrichment jobs complete. snapshot() Export a JSONL snapshot of memory.

docs.title: Entity types
docs.text: These strings are the canonical values used in recall_entity(), ingest_relationship(), and the entity index. Spell them exactly as shown.

docs.title: CTI and IOC types (regex-extracted, no LLM required)
docs.text: Entity type Example cve CVE-2024-1234 intrusion_set APT28, UNC4990, FIN7 actor Lazarus, Sandworm, Volt Typhoon tool Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, BloodHound campaign Operation Aurora attack_pattern T1059, T1059.001 ipv4 IPv4 address domain Registered domain url HTTP/HTTPS URL md5 32-character hex hash sha1 40-character hex hash sha256 64-character hex hash email Email address

docs.title: Conversational types (LLM NER, requires a configured LLM provider)
docs.text: Entity type Description person Named person in non-threat-actor context location Place name organization Named organization event Named event activity Described activity temporal Time expression

docs.title: Lookup aliases
docs.text: recall_actor() searches actor, threat_actor, and intrusion_set in one call. The actor and threat_actor types are interchangeable for lookup but intrusion_set is preferred for APT/UNC/FIN-style designations.

docs.title: Knowledge graph relationship types
docs.text: ZettelForge 2.8.0 writes these built-in relationship labels and returns them from get_entity_relationships() and traverse_graph(). You can also pass them to ingest_relationship(). See the KG Edge Schema reference for the complete taxonomy.

docs.title: CTI and IOC relationship types
docs.text: Relationship Meaning MENTIONED_IN Entity appears in a note USES_TOOL Actor or campaign uses a tool EXPLOITS_CVE Actor or tool exploits a CVE TARGETS_ASSET Actor or tool targets an asset CONDUCTS_CAMPAIGN Actor conducts a campaign USES_TECHNIQUE Actor uses an ATT&CK technique IMPLEMENTS Malware implements an ATT&CK technique

docs.title: Temporal and note-lifecycle relationship types
docs.text: Relationship Meaning SUPERSEDES Note supersedes another note

docs.title: Conversational relationship types
docs.text:
These are written by the LLM enrichment path and require a configured LLM provider.

Relationship Meaning AFFILIATED_WITH Person affiliated with an organization ATTENDED Person attended an event LOCATED_AT Person or organization at a location PARTICIPATES_IN Person participates in an activity HELD_AT Event held at a location ORGANIZED_BY Event organized by an organization OCCURRED_ON Event occurred at a temporal point BASED_IN Organization based in a location

docs.title: Epistemic tier values
docs.text:
The tier field on MemoryNote.metadata uses single uppercase letters.

Value Meaning A Authoritative — from a primary, verified source B Operational — derived, processed, or synthesized C Support — background, context, or low-confidence

docs.title: TLP values
docs.text:
In ZettelForge 2.8.0, MemoryNote.metadata.tlp is a free-form string with an empty-string default. The shipped schema documents the following values, and the SQLite backend stores the string without normalizing it:

Value Role in ZettelForge 2.8.0 "" (empty string) Schema and SQLite default WHITE Documented schema value; not validated GREEN Documented schema value; not validated AMBER Documented schema value; not validated RED Documented schema value; not validated

TLP policy enforcement is in progress

ZettelForge 2.8.0 does not validate, rank, or enforce TLP values. Use the labels above consistently, but enforce sharing policy outside ZettelForge until a public policy layer ships.

docs.title: Architecture terms
docs.text: Term Use knowledge graph The entity relationship store. Two words, no hyphen in prose. background worker The thread that drains the enrichment queue. Not "agent". enrichment LLM-driven causal extraction, NER, and note evolution. Not "processing". blended retrieval Combined vector similarity plus graph traversal. Not "hybrid retrieval". fast path The write path that returns before LLM enrichment completes. two-phase extraction Phase 1 (score facts) plus Phase 2 (decide ADD/UPDATE/NOOP). Hyphenated as a compound modifier. backend Storage backend (SQLite or TypeDB). Lowercase in prose; SQLiteBackend as a class name.

docs.title: Storage backends
docs.text: Term Use sqlite The default backend. Lowercase in config values; "SQLite" in prose. typedb The TypeDB 3.x backend. Lowercase in config values; "TypeDB" in prose.

docs.title: Synthesis format values
docs.text:
format argument to synthesize() and POST /api/synthesize.

Value Availability direct_answer Available in ZettelForge 2.8.0 synthesized_brief In progress. ZettelForge 2.8.0 accepts the value but falls back to direct_answer; the current ThreatRecall.ai endpoint uses brief or detailed instead. timeline_analysis In progress. ZettelForge 2.8.0 accepts the value but falls back to direct_answer; the current ThreatRecall.ai endpoint uses brief or detailed instead. relationship_map In progress. ZettelForge 2.8.0 accepts the value but falls back to direct_answer; the current ThreatRecall.ai endpoint uses brief or detailed instead.

docs.title: Web API reference
docs.text:
ZettelForge 2.8.0 ships a FastAPI backend (web/app.py) that exposes the memory system over HTTP and serves the management SPA.

Prerequisites: Install ZettelForge 2.8.0 with its web optional dependencies and choose an unused loopback port. The verified command below uses port 8089:

python3 -m web.app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8089

The server reports itself as ZettelForge v2.8.0. All paths under /api/ are guarded; the SPA at / is not.

Current in-progress endpoint

/api/sync is not ready in ZettelForge OSS. The endpoint returns HTTP 501, but the current runtime response body still uses a legacy extension-package error string that is pending cleanup. This page documents the status code and product boundary without reproducing that deprecated package name.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every /api/* route depends on a single guard. Supply your key in either header:

X-API-Key: <key>
Authorization: Bearer <key>

Behavior depends on ZETTELFORGE_WEB_API_KEY:

Condition Result Key set, request matches Allowed (constant-time compare) Key set, missing or wrong 401 Valid API key required Key unset, caller is loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost) Allowed — single-tenant local mode Key unset, caller is non-loopback 503 Set ZETTELFORGE_WEB_API_KEY before exposing the web API

Binding to 0.0.0.0 or :: without a key set is refused at startup. Set the key before exposing the API beyond localhost.

docs.title: Rate and write limits
docs.text:
Control Env var Default Requests per minute, per key/IP ZETTELFORGE_WEB_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE 60 Concurrent writes ZETTELFORGE_WEB_WRITE_CONCURRENCY 2 Max query length ZETTELFORGE_WEB_MAX_QUERY_CHARS 1000 Max content length ZETTELFORGE_WEB_MAX_CONTENT_CHARS 50000 Max k ZETTELFORGE_WEB_MAX_K 50 Max sync limit ZETTELFORGE_WEB_MAX_SYNC_LIMIT 200

Exceeding the rate limit returns 429 Rate limit exceeded. Write endpoints return 429 when the write semaphore is exhausted.

docs.title: POST /api/recall
docs.text:
Retrieve notes for a query.

Request:

Field Type Default Constraints query string required 1–1000 chars k int 10 1–50 domain string null ≤100 chars

Response:

{
  "query": "APT28 infrastructure",
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "...",
      "content": "...",
      "domain": "cti",
      "tier": "a",
      "confidence": 0.0,
      "created_at": "...",
      "entities": ["..."],
      "context": "..."
    }
  ],
  "count": 1,
  "latency_ms": 42
}

content is truncated to 500 chars and entities to 10 per result.

docs.title: POST /api/remember
docs.text:
Store one note.

Field Type Default Constraints content string required 1–50000 chars domain string cti 1–100 chars source_type string manual 1–100 chars source_ref string "" ≤500 chars evolve bool true

Response: { "note_id", "status", "entities", "latency_ms" }. Returns 429 Write capacity exhausted; retry shortly when the write semaphore is full.

docs.title: POST /api/ingest
docs.text:
Bulk version of remember.

Request: { "items": [ { "content", "source_type"="manual", "domain"="cti", "evolve"=true } ] } — 1 to 100 items.

Response:

{
  "total": 3,
  "succeeded": 2,
  "failed": 1,
  "results": [
    { "note_id": "...", "status": "...", "entities": ["..."], "success": true, "error": null }
  ]
}

Per-item failures (including skipped when write capacity is exhausted) are reported in results; the call itself returns 200.

docs.title: POST /api/synthesize
docs.text:
Generate an answer from retrieved notes.

Field Type Default Constraints query string required 1–1000 chars format string direct_answer one of direct_answer, synthesized_brief, timeline_analysis, relationship_map k int 10 1–50

An unsupported format returns 400 Unsupported synthesis format. Response: { "query", "format", "synthesis", "sources_count", "latency_ms" }.

Synthesis format availability

In ZettelForge OSS, the extended formats (synthesized_brief, timeline_analysis, relationship_map) return a direct-answer-shaped synthesis payload. The HTTP format field still echoes the requested format. ThreatRecall.ai SaaS exposes its own authenticated synthesis endpoint for hosted recall workflows. synthesize also depends on a configured LLM provider; without one it returns a well-formed result with no answer.

docs.title: GET /api/graph/nodes
docs.text: { "nodes": [ { "id", "label", "type", "tier", "aliases", "confidence", "created_at" } ], "count" }

Paginated entity index.

Query parameters: offset (≥0, default 0), limit (1–500, default 50), type, tier, q (substring filter on entity value).

Response: { "entities": [...], "total", "offset", "limit" }.

docs.text: { "total_notes", "entity_count", "graph_node_count", "graph_edge_count" }

docs.text: { "version", "notes", "edition" } — used by the SPA header.

docs.title: GET /api/telemetry
docs.text: Aggregated counters from today's telemetry JSONL: total_queries, queries_today, recall_count, synthesis_count, syntheses_today, avg_latency_ms, p50_ms, p95_ms, top_intents. Returns zeroed fields when no telemetry file exists yet.

docs.text: Recent telemetry entries. Query parameters: limit (1–500, default 100), days (1–30, default 5). Returns a JSON array.

docs.text: Tail of the structlog file. Query parameters: lines (1–10000, default 100), level (optional filter). Response: { "logs": [...], "truncated" }. Returns an empty list with an error field when no log file is configured.

docs.title: Server-sent event streams
docs.text:
Path Stream GET /api/logs/stream Tails the structlog file (text/event-stream) GET /api/telemetry/stream Tails today's telemetry JSONL (text/event-stream)

Both emit data: <line>\n\n frames and handle log rotation.

docs.title: GET /api/config
docs.text: Returns the full resolved config as JSON. Sensitive keys (such as api_key, password, and token) are recursively redacted to ***.

docs.title: GET /api/config/meta
docs.text: { "restart_required_fields": [...] } — the dotted config paths that require a process restart, including backend, embedding.provider, llm.provider, llm.model, storage.data_dir, and the logging fields.

docs.title: PUT /api/config
docs.text:
Apply config changes in memory. Accepts nested or dotted keys ({"retrieval.default_k": 5}). Response:

{
  "applied": ["retrieval.default_k"],
  "pending_restart": ["llm.model"],
  "message": "Config updated in-memory. Some changes require a restart."
}

Fields in restart_required_fields are reported under pending_restart and take effect only after a restart.

docs.title: POST /api/sync
docs.text:
OpenCTI synchronization is in progress in ZettelForge OSS. In the current OSS runtime this endpoint returns HTTP 501. The response body is pending cleanup because it still uses a legacy extension-package error string.

ThreatRecall.ai SaaS provides STIX 2.1 import/export workflows for exchange with OpenCTI and MISP. Native OpenCTI pull/push sync remains in progress. See Two products, one core for the OSS-versus-SaaS split.

GET /api/edition reports the running build's capability set in its features map. On an OSS install edition is community. opencti_integration, typedb_stix_ontology, alias_resolution_typedb, sigma_generation, context_injection, and multi_tenant_auth resolve to false; they are not available in ZettelForge OSS through this API. Core features such as vector search, blended retrieval, temporal graph queries, graph traversal, report ingestion, and direct-answer synthesis resolve to true.
