docs.title: YARA schema reference
docs.text:
Use this page to look up the ZettelForge YARA parser, CCCS metadata validation, entity mapping, ingest API, and command-line interface. The reference covers ZettelForge 2.8.0, released under the MIT license.

Modules: zettelforge.yara, zettelforge.yara.parser, zettelforge.yara.cccs_metadata, zettelforge.yara.entities, zettelforge.yara.tags, zettelforge.yara.ingest

In progress

Parsing, core metadata validation, entity mapping, persistence, and dry-run ingestion work in ZettelForge 2.8.0. Modifier flags, several optional CCCS validators, reference mapping, strict live-ingest exit status, dry-run symlink protection, and CLI explainer integration remain incomplete. See Current limitations.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: You need ZettelForge 2.8.0 and Python 3.10 or later. Use Configure YARA ingestion for a task-oriented import procedure. Read Detection rules schema for the shared Sigma and YARA model.

docs.title: Public exports
docs.text:
zettelforge.yara exports these names:

Name Kind Purpose YaraRule dataclass YARA-specific DetectionRule subtype YaraParseError exception Reports file stat and size errors YaraValidationError exception Reserved validation exception; the 2.8.0 APIs return ValidationResult instead of raising it parse_yara function Parses YARA source text parse_file function Reads and parses one rule file validate_metadata function Validates flattened metadata at a selected tier rule_to_entities function Builds a YaraRule and relation dictionaries resolve_yara_tag function Resolves supported inline tags to typed entities ingest_rule function Persists the first rule from one input ingest_rules_dir function Walks and ingests a rule directory

zettelforge.yara.parser.parse_text is a legacy alias for parse_yara. It is available from the parser submodule but is not a package-level export.

docs.title: Processing layers
docs.text: Layer Module Responsibility Parser yara.parser Wrap Plyara and normalize parsed dictionaries Metadata yara.cccs_metadata / yara.schemas Load the CCCS metadata definitions and apply the implemented validators Entity yara.entities / yara.tags Map a parsed dictionary to YaraRule and relation dictionaries Ingest yara.ingest Store each rule as a memory note and write knowledge-graph edges

docs.title: Vendored CCCS schemas
docs.text:
ZettelForge packages two CCCS YARA metadata files in src/zettelforge/yara/schemas/:

File Purpose CCCS_YARA.yml Declares metadata fields, formats, uniqueness, optionality, and validator names CCCS_YARA_values.yml Declares allowed status, sharing, category, malware-type, actor-type, and hash patterns

The YAML files come from the Cyber Centre's CCCS-Yara project and retain its MIT license. ZettelForge does not vendor the upstream validator_functions.py; cccs_metadata.py implements the validation logic locally. The module loads both YAML files at import time, so a missing or unreadable file prevents the module from importing.

docs.title: Metadata validation
docs.text:
Signature: validate_metadata(rule_meta: dict[str, Any], tier: Tier = 'warn') -> ValidationResult

ValidationResult contains three fields:

Field Type Meaning accepted bool Whether the selected tier accepts the metadata warnings list[str] Non-blocking missing-field and value findings errors list[str] Blocking strict-tier findings

docs.title: Validation tiers
docs.text:
Tier Behavior warn Records missing required fields and invalid values as warnings; always sets accepted=True strict Records missing or invalid required fields as errors and sets accepted=False; invalid optional fields remain warnings non_cccs Skips every check and returns accepted=True with empty warning and error lists

Strict-tier ingest drops a rule when its entity is not marked strict. Warn-tier ingest keeps the rule and records the findings in YaraRule.extra.

docs.title: Fields required by ZettelForge strict mode
docs.text:
ZettelForge combines two CCCS optionality classes into one strict gate. It requires every optional: No field and every optional: Optional field because the local validator does not generate missing values.

Field CCCS optionality Implemented format or values id Optional Base62 text with at least 16 characters fingerprint Optional 40–64 hexadecimal characters version Optional Two numeric components, such as 1.0 modified Optional YYYY-MM-DD text status No TESTING, RELEASED, or DEPRECATED sharing No One of the supported TLP strings below source No Any non-empty value; uppercase is a convention, not a validation rule author No Whole value matches [A-Za-z0-9_.@+-]+ description No Non-empty after trimming category No INFO, EXPLOIT, TECHNIQUE, TOOL, or MALWARE

Supported sharing values are:

  • TLP:CLEAR and TLP:CLEAR//COMMERCIAL
  • TLP:WHITE and TLP:WHITE//COMMERCIAL
  • TLP:GREEN and TLP:GREEN//COMMERCIAL
  • TLP:AMBER and TLP:AMBER//COMMERCIAL
  • TLP:AMBER+STRICT and TLP:AMBER+STRICT//COMMERCIAL

TLP:WHITE remains accepted alongside TLP:CLEAR for compatibility with existing rules.

docs.title: Optional fields with implemented validation
docs.text:
Field Accepted value date YYYY-MM-DD text malware_type One of the values in Malware type values actor_type APT, CRIMEWARE, or FIN hash 32-, 40-, or 64-character hexadecimal value mitre_att One TA####, T####, T####.###, M####, G####, or S#### identifier

An invalid optional value produces a warning in both warn and strict mode; it does not make strict validation fail. The entity converter separately splits comma- and semicolon-delimited mitre_att text, but the metadata validator accepts only one identifier per value.

docs.title: Declared fields without implemented validation
docs.text:
The vendored schema declares validators for these optional fields, but ZettelForge 2.8.0 accepts their values without applying those validators:

Field Format declared by the vendored schema score Integer percentage minimum_yara x.x version actor Actor name mitre_group ATT&CK group alias report Linked report reference Free-form external reference category child metadata Category-specific uppercase value

The schema also declares unvalidated fields such as tags, vol_script, al_*, credit, and original_*. Unknown metadata keys pass through without a warning.

docs.title: Malware type values
docs.text:
The implemented malware_type validator accepts:

ADWARE, APT, BACKDOOR, BANKER, BOOTKIT, BOT, BROWSER-HIJACKER, BRUTEFORCER, CLICKFRAUD, CRYPTOMINER, DDOS, DOWNLOADER, DROPPER, EXPLOITKIT, FAKEAV, HACKTOOL, INFOSTEALER, KEYLOGGER, LOADER, OBFUSCATOR, POS, PROXY, RAT, RANSOMWARE, REVERSE-PROXY, ROOTKIT, SCANNER, SCAREWARE, SPAMMER, TROJAN, VIRUS, WIPER, WEBSHELL, and WORM.

docs.title: parse_yara
docs.text:
Signature: parse_yara(text: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

parse_yara parses source text into one dictionary per rule. It protects a module-level plyara.Plyara instance with _PARSER_LOCK, clears the parser before and after every call, flattens Plyara's metadata list into meta, and carves raw_rule from the source line range.

The normalizer always adds these keys:

Key Type Meaning meta dict Flattened metadata; the last duplicate key wins tags list[str] Inline tags, or an empty list raw_rule str Source text between Plyara's start and stop lines

Plyara supplies the remaining rule-dependent keys, including rule_name, metadata, strings, condition_terms, raw_condition, raw_strings, raw_meta, start_line, stop_line, and scopes. ZettelForge also copies parser-level imports into a rule when Plyara omits them from that rule.

Plyara syntax failures surface as ValueError with a plyara parse error message.

docs.title: parse_file
docs.text:
Signature: parse_file(path: str | Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

parse_file stats the path, rejects files larger than MAX_RULE_FILE_BYTES = 1_048_576, reads UTF-8 text, and delegates to parse_yara.

Failure Exception Path cannot be statted YaraParseError File exceeds 1,048,576 bytes YaraParseError Plyara rejects the text ValueError UTF-8 read fails after a successful stat The underlying read or decode exception

YaraParseError extends ValueError.

docs.title: DetectionRule
docs.text:
YaraRule extends zettelforge.detection.base.DetectionRule.

Field Type YARA mapping rule_id str CCCS id, or yara_ plus the first 16 content-hash characters title str Parsed rule name source_format str yara content_sha256 str SHA-256 of raw_rule, or a stable fallback projection description str \| None CCCS description author str \| None CCCS author date str \| None CCCS date modified str \| None CCCS modified references list[str] One CCCS report value when present; reference is not mapped tags list[str] Raw inline YARA tags level str \| None Remains None status str \| None Lowercase CCCS status tlp str \| None CCCS sharing value license str \| None Remains None source_repo str \| None Remains None source_path str \| None Remains None; directory ingest writes the path into the note body extra dict[str, Any] Validation and parser details described below

docs.title: YaraRule
docs.text:
Field Type Mapping cccs_id str \| None CCCS id fingerprint str \| None CCCS fingerprint category str \| None CCCS category technique_tag str \| None CCCS technique cccs_version str \| None String form of CCCS version hash_of_sample list[str] One or more CCCS hash values rule_name str \| None Parsed rule name is_private bool Remains False in 2.8.0 even when Plyara reports a private scope is_global bool Remains False in 2.8.0 even when Plyara reports a global scope imports list[str] Parsed YARA module imports condition str \| None Trimmed raw condition

extra always contains cccs_compliant, cccs_warnings, cccs_errors, condition_terms, and source_line_range. It also contains source and malware_type when present. If metadata supplies actor_type without an actor name, extra contains actor_type and the converter emits no actor relation.

docs.title: Entity conversion
docs.text:
Signature: rule_to_entities(rule: dict[str, Any], *, tier: str = 'warn') -> tuple[YaraRule, list[dict[str, Any]]]

The function validates rule['meta'] at the requested tier and returns a YaraRule plus relation dictionaries. It returns the entity even when strict validation fails; the ingest layer decides whether to drop it.

zettelforge.yara.entities.from_rule_dict(rule) is a compatibility wrapper that calls rule_to_entities at the default warn tier. It is not a package-level export.

Each relation dictionary contains:

Key Value from_type YaraRule from_value Source rule identifier rel ZettelForge relation name to_type Target entity type to_value Target entity identifier properties Relation metadata

docs.title: Emitted relations
docs.text:
Relation Target type Emitted when detects AttackPattern CCCS mitre_att contains a token, including TA, T, M, G, or S identifiers detects AttackPattern An inline tag resolves as a technique attributed_to ThreatActor CCCS actor contains a name tagged_with YaraTag CCCS technique contains a value tagged_with YaraTag An inline tag resolves as a category or free-form tag references_cve Vulnerability An inline tag resolves as a CVE

The CCCS mitre_att mapper uppercases and splits list, comma-delimited, and semicolon-delimited values. It maps every token to AttackPattern; it does not distinguish group, software, or tactic identifiers.

docs.title: Tag resolution
docs.text:
Signature: resolve_yara_tag(tag: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, str]]

Input pattern Returned entity and properties T1218, attack.T1218, or attack_T1218 AttackPattern with technique_id='T1218' attack.T1059.003 AttackPattern with technique_id='T1059.003' CVE_2021_44228 or CVE-2021-44228 Vulnerability with canonical cve_id Known category token YaraTag with namespace category and an uppercase name Any other value YaraTag with namespace freeform and the trimmed input

Known category tokens are APT, CRIME, CRIMEWARE, EXPL, HKTL, MAL, MALWARE, PUA, RAT, RANSOM, RANSOMWARE, SUSP, VULN, and WEBSHELL. Matching is case-insensitive.

Each inline tag emits one relation. A technique or CVE tag emits its typed relation instead of an additional raw-tag relation.

docs.title: ingest_rule
docs.text:
Signature: ingest_rule(rule_source, mm=None, *, domain='detection', tier='warn', sync=True) -> tuple[MemoryNote | None, list[dict]]

Parameter Accepted value Default Behavior rule_source Dictionary, YARA text, path string, or Path required Normalizes the input and ingests only the first parsed rule mm MemoryManager-compatible object None Raises ValueError when omitted or None domain string detection Stored note domain tier strict, warn, or non_cccs warn Controls CCCS validation sync boolean True Controls inline enrichment in MemoryManager.remember

Strict rejection returns (None, relations). A new accepted rule becomes a memory note with source_type='yara'. The generated source reference is yara:<rule_id>:<first-12-content-hash-characters>.

If the store already contains that source reference, the function returns the existing note and newly computed relations without persisting a duplicate.

docs.title: ingest_rules_dir
docs.text:
Signature: ingest_rules_dir(path, mm=None, *, glob='**/*.yar', tier='warn', domain='detection', bulk=False, flush_timeout=None) -> dict[str, Any]

The return dictionary has ingested, skipped, and errors fields. A missing root returns {'ingested': 0, 'skipped': 0, 'errors': ['path does not exist: ...']} instead of raising.

The default glob checks both .yar and .yara files. A custom glob replaces that pair. The function records parse and per-rule failures in errors, counts strict rejections and idempotent hits as skipped, and continues the walk.

When bulk=True, the function calls each rule ingest with sync=False and calls mm.flush(timeout=flush_timeout) once after the walk when mm exposes a flush method. A false flush result produces a warning log and does not add a return error.

docs.title: Directory security controls
docs.text: Control Behavior File size parse_file rejects files larger than 1,048,576 bytes Symlinks ingest_rules_dir skips symlinked files Root containment ingest_rules_dir skips resolved paths outside the requested root

docs.title: Knowledge-graph edge persistence
docs.text:
Before persistence, ingest adds these properties unless the relation already supplies them:

Property Value edge_type detection source yara_ingest

If one edge write raises an exception, ZettelForge logs yara_edge_persist_failed and continues with the next relation.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The verified dry-run invocation against the v2.8.0 release fixture is:

python3 -m zettelforge.yara.ingest tests/fixtures/yara/technique_loader.yar --dry-run
Argument Default Description path required One .yar file or a directory --tier warn strict, warn, or non_cccs --dry-run off Parses, validates, and maps without persistence --domain detection Memory domain for persisted notes --json off Emits JSON instead of the human-readable summary

The successful command writes this stdout and exits 0:

[warn] MemoryModule  (technique_loader.yar)  relations=2  mitre=T1218
    warn: missing required CCCS field: id
    warn: missing required CCCS field: fingerprint
    warn: missing required CCCS field: modified

The ingest module invocation emits a non-fatal runpy warning on stderr because zettelforge.yara.__init__ imports ingest before Python executes it as a module. The command still runs.

Dry-run mode returns exit 1 for parse failures and strict-tier rejection. Live mode returns exit 1 when the result contains errors or the input path is missing. In 2.8.0, a strict-tier live rejection increments skipped but leaves errors empty, so the command prints ingested=0 skipped=1 errors=0 and incorrectly exits 0.

The CLI does not invoke the LLM rule explainer in 2.8.0.

docs.title: Quick reference example
docs.text:
This self-contained example parses a rule and inspects its entity relations without writing data:

from zettelforge.yara import parse_yara, rule_to_entities

yara_text = """rule CommandShell : APT T1218 CVE_2021_44228 {
    strings:
        $cmd = "cmd.exe"
    condition:
        $cmd
}
"""

rule_dict = parse_yara(yara_text)[0]
entity, relations = rule_to_entities(rule_dict, tier="non_cccs")
print(entity.rule_id, entity.rule_name, entity.extra["cccs_compliant"])
print([(edge["rel"], edge["to_value"]) for edge in relations])

Output:

yara_bb08e39bbce9a1f8 CommandShell non_cccs
[('tagged_with', 'APT'), ('detects', 'T1218'), ('references_cve', 'CVE-2021-44228')]

docs.title: Current limitations
docs.text:
These ZettelForge 2.8.0 behaviors are in progress:

  • Plyara records private and global modifiers in scopes, but entity conversion leaves YaraRule.is_private and YaraRule.is_global false.
  • The optional CCCS validators listed under Declared fields without implemented validation do not run.
  • The metadata validator accepts one mitre_att identifier, while entity conversion also splits compound values. The converter maps every resulting identifier type to AttackPattern.
  • YaraRule.references maps report but ignores reference.
  • Strict-tier rejection in live CLI mode exits 0 when no separate ingest error occurs.
  • CLI dry-run directory traversal follows matching symlinked rule files; the ingest_rules_dir persistence path skips them.
  • YaraValidationError is exported but no YARA 2.8.0 public function raises it.
  • The CLI parses, validates, maps, and persists rules, but it does not run the LLM rule explainer.

docs.title: RFC-001: Conversational Entity Extractor
docs.text: Field Value Author Patrick Roland Status Partially Implemented Created 2026-04-09 Last updated 2026-07-27 ZettelForge version v2.7.0 Related RFCs RFC-002 Universal LLM Provider

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ZettelForge's entity extractor recognizes CTI entities: CVEs, APT groups, tools, campaigns, IOCs. The LOCOMO benchmark tests conversational memory — person names, locations, hobbies, life events, and temporal references. Those entity types were invisible to the regex-only extractor.

At v1.5.0, ZettelForge scored 15% on LOCOMO. Root cause analysis identified entity extraction mismatch as the primary blocker: retrieved context contained the answer (75.9% keyword presence), but graph traversal returned nothing because no recognized entities matched LOCOMO queries. Multi-hop and temporal accuracy were 0%.

docs.title: Proposal
docs.text:
Replace regex-only entity extraction with a hybrid pipeline:

  • Regex fast-path for CTI and IOC types (reliable, deterministic, no LLM required)
  • LLM NER for conversational types (person, location, organization, event, activity, temporal) where regex fails

This gives 19 entity types total: 6 CTI, 7 IOC, 6 conversational.

Target: 80%+ LOCOMO accuracy.

docs.title: Entity types (Steps 1–3 — complete)
docs.text:
EntityExtractor in entity_indexer.py is the single source of truth for all extraction. NoteConstructor.extract_entities() delegates to it. The 19-type schema is live:

Category Entity types Extraction method CTI cve, intrusion_set, actor, tool, campaign, attack_pattern Regex IOC (STIX cyber observables) ipv4, domain, url, md5, sha1, sha256, email Regex Conversational person, location, organization, event, activity, temporal Regex fallback plus background LLM NER when enabled

The IOC types were not in the original proposal — they were added during implementation to support CTIBench and real-world CTI workflows.

For entity type reference and the get_entity_relationships() / traverse_graph() API, see KG Edge Schema and Memory Manager API.

docs.title: Hash false-positive filter (complete)
docs.text: Hash IOC patterns (md5/sha1/sha256) match any 32/40/64-character hex string, producing false positives on git commit SHAs and code assignments. EntityExtractor._CODE_CONTEXT_PATTERN detects code or VCS context per line and excludes all hex strings on matching lines from final results. This is a compiled re.VERBOSE pattern that handles assignments, commit entries, merge lines, code fences, and function definitions.

docs.title: _PERSON_PATTERN and _LOCATION_PATTERN (complete, limited)
docs.text:
Two regex patterns handle conversational entities without an LLM call:

  • _PERSON_PATTERN matches dialogue format Name: text (e.g., transcript speaker labels), with a stopword filter excluding 40+ common words and day/month names.
  • _LOCATION_PATTERN matches 40+ major world cities by name.

These are supplementary. They do not cover implicit references ("my friend from college") or locations not in the hardcoded list.

docs.title: extract_llm() and LLM NER enrichment (complete; background path active)
docs.text:
EntityExtractor.extract_llm() is implemented and functional when called directly. It calls the configured LLM provider with a structured JSON prompt, isolates input to 2,000 characters, uses get_config().llm.max_tokens_ner (default 2500) with temperature=0.0, and retries once on JSON parse failure with json_mode=True and temperature=0.3. On exception, it returns an empty dict and logs exc_info=True.

The foreground remember() path still indexes the note with extract_all(use_llm=False) for deterministic writes. After that write, MemoryManager.remember() dispatches an llm_ner enrichment job when both enrichment.enabled and llm_ner.enabled are true. Both default to true and can be disabled with ZETTELFORGE_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED=false or ZETTELFORGE_LLM_NER_ENABLED=false. _run_llm_ner() calls extract_llm(), then writes any new entity mappings into the storage backend and the legacy JSON EntityIndexer.

Benchmark ingestion disables enrichment with ZETTELFORGE_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED=false, so LOCOMO runs do not exercise LLM NER unless you intentionally override that benchmark default.

docs.title: EntityIndexer persistence (complete)
docs.text:
EntityIndexer maintains an inverted index: {entity_type -> {entity_value -> Set[note_id]}}. Writes are batched via a 5-second threading.Timer (deferred flush). An atexit handler flushes on process exit. build() reindexes all notes synchronously with regex-only extraction.

As of v2.2.0, entity data exists in two stores: entity_index.json (the primary runtime store) and a SQLite entity_index table. The two are not kept in sync by a single authoritative writer. This is a known inconsistency.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
tests/test_conversational_entities.py has 27 tests across 8 classes (5 more than the 22 named at RFC write time; TestFreeTextPersonNotExtracted was added after the adversarial review):

Class Tests Notes TestRegexExtraction 5 CVE, actor, tool, campaign, no-match TestLLMExtraction 3 Runs against the mock LLM provider TestHybridExtraction 2 Runs against the mock LLM provider TestNERParsing 3 JSON parse logic with mocked output TestNoteConstructorDelegation 2 Delegation wiring TestInferEntityType 5 CVE, APT, tool, type hints, unknown TestEntityIndexerConversational 3 All types present, add/lookup, cross-type search TestFreeTextPersonNotExtracted 4 Stopword filter regression tests (added post-RFC)

Additional coverage now exists outside this file: tests/test_basic.py::TestEntityExtractor covers IOC extraction and the git-SHA hash false-positive filter, and tests/test_entity_indexer_races.py covers the RFC-001 Warning 4, 5, and 6 fixes for atomic save, remove_note(), and concurrent save/mutation. The remaining test gap is live-provider LLM NER quality; current LLM NER tests prove parser and wiring behavior with a mock provider, not extraction quality from a real model.

docs.title: What did not ship
docs.text:
Step 4 — production SynthesisGenerator in benchmark. locomo_benchmark.py now calls a benchmark-local _synthesize_answer() helper after retrieval. That helper uses Ollama's /api/generate endpoint with SYNTH_MODEL defaulting to qwen2.5:3b, then falls back to relevant-sentence extraction when the LLM call fails. The original RFC goal of wiring the production SynthesisGenerator into the benchmark has not shipped.

Foreground LLM NER activation. The deterministic foreground indexing path still uses extract_all(use_llm=False). LLM NER activation now exists as a background enrichment job, not as an inline use_llm=True call inside remember() or NoteConstructor.

Batch LLM NER. LLM NER jobs run one note at a time through the enrichment worker. No batch API or batched prompt path has shipped.

EntityIndexer backend unification. The JSON/SQLite dual-write inconsistency has not been resolved.

docs.title: LOCOMO benchmark results
docs.text:
The RFC targeted 80%+ LOCOMO accuracy. Actual results:

Version Score Judge Primary driver v1.5.0 15% Keyword overlap Baseline (regex-only CTI) v2.0.0 18% Keyword overlap Entity schema expansion v2.1.1 22% Ollama cloud model Supersession perf fix, file locking, cloud judge v2.7.0 7% Keyword judge Regression vs v2.1.1 Ollama judge; methodology change

The 80% target was not achieved. Analysis:

  • Entity extraction alone is insufficient. The benchmark now has a local focused-answer helper, but it does not use the production SynthesisGenerator, and the fallback still evaluates extracted context snippets when no synthesis LLM is available.
  • The 3B model ceiling. Qwen2.5-3B handles common entities adequately but struggles with implicit references and abstract events. LOCOMO relies heavily on these.
  • LLM NER is activated only through background enrichment and is disabled during the deterministic benchmark path. The core RFC value proposition, LLM-powered conversational NER improving multi-hop and temporal accuracy, remains unmeasured in the LOCOMO benchmark.
  • Most of the v2.1.1 gain came from performance fixes and a better judge, not from entity extraction.

The v2.7.0 7% keyword-judge baseline is not directly comparable to the v2.1.1 22% Ollama-judge result. The methodology change (keyword judge vs LLM judge) accounts for most of the apparent regression. See Reproduce Benchmarks for how to replicate either result.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Accepted (2026-04-09). Adversarial review completed 2026-04-16. Two blockers identified and actioned: load() log event name corrected; attack_pattern regex capture group fixed. Remaining findings documented as open issues.

Status as of v2.7.0: Partially Implemented. Steps 1–3 are complete. LLM NER activation exists as background enrichment. Step 4's production SynthesisGenerator benchmark integration is not complete.

docs.title: Adversarial review findings (2026-04-16)
docs.text: # Severity Finding Status 1 BLOCKER use_llm=True never called — LLM NER is dead code Fixed as background enrichment; foreground path remains regex-only 2 BLOCKER load() logs entity_index_save_failed instead of load_failed Fixed 3 WARNING attack_pattern regex lacked capture group Fixed 4 WARNING save() truncates before flock — race condition Fixed 5 WARNING remove_note() deletes entity type keys Fixed 6 WARNING _flush_sync() not thread-safe on self.index Fixed 7 WARNING extract_all(use_llm=True) overwrites regex results Fixed 8 WARNING No tests for IOCs, hash filter, remove_note, search_entities Fixed except live-provider LLM NER quality coverage 9 WARNING Root cause analysis omitted LLM NER not activated Fixed in RFC 10 NIT Test count stated as 18, actual was 23 (now 27 in v2.7.0) Fixed in RFC

docs.title: Recommendations for future work
docs.text:
1. Measure background LLM NER impact on LOCOMO with enrichment enabled and a reachable real LLM provider.
  2. Replace the benchmark-local _synthesize_answer() helper with the production SynthesisGenerator, then re-run LOCOMO with the same judge and dataset.
  3. Add mock-based NER regression tests that cover extract_llm() without a live model. TestNERParsing already covers parse logic; extend to the full extraction path.
  4. Unify EntityIndexer storage to write through StorageBackend and eliminate the JSON/SQLite dual-write inconsistency.
  5. Evaluate RFC-002 (Universal LLM Provider) impact: once a larger model is accessible through a stable provider interface, re-run LOCOMO to measure the NER quality ceiling independent of the 3B model constraint.

docs.title: RFC-002: Universal LLM Provider Interface
docs.text:
RFC-002 separates ZettelForge's LLM-dependent workflows from specific model backends. The provider infrastructure shipped in v2.3.0 and remains present in v2.8.0. RFC-012 later replaced the proposed provider-specific cloud adapters with the optional LiteLLM provider; per-call provider selection did not ship.

Use this design record to understand the decision and its consequences. For current setup instructions, use Configuration reference. To add a provider, use Build an extension.

Field Value Author Patrick Roland Status Accepted — provider infrastructure implemented; later phases superseded or unimplemented Created 2026-04-16 Last verified 2026-08-08 Verified release ZettelForge v2.8.0 Related RFCs RFC-001 Conversational Entity Extractor · RFC-012 LiteLLM Unified Provider

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ZettelForge originally selected between its local GGUF backend and Ollama inside one client module. That design tied extraction, classification, enrichment, and synthesis to backend-specific configuration and failure handling. Adding another backend required changes in the shared client path.

The design needed to preserve the public generation call while giving each backend one implementation boundary. It also needed to keep the cloud-routing SDK optional so the core package remained usable without it.

docs.title: Decision drivers
docs.text:
• Keep LLM call sites independent of the selected backend.
  • Preserve the existing public generation call.
  • Keep the cloud-routing dependency optional.
  • Let third-party packages add providers without changing ZettelForge source.
  • Surface permanent configuration failures instead of hiding them behind fallback behavior.
  • Preserve the existing local-to-Ollama recoverable fallback path.

docs.title: Proposal
docs.text:
Route generation through three layers:

  1. The public zettelforge.llm_client.generate() function reads the active configuration.
  2. A registry resolves a provider name to one cached provider instance.
  3. The provider implements the LLMProvider protocol and performs generation.

The protocol uses typing.Protocol and carries the runtime_checkable marker. Callers can opt into isinstance() checks, but the registry does not validate protocol conformance during registration. A provider exposes a short name and a synchronous generate() method; it does not inherit from a ZettelForge base class.

The registry owns registration, lookup, instance caching, and reset behavior. It protects registration and first-time construction with a lock. Unknown names and duplicate registrations raise ValueError.

docs.title: Shipped result
docs.text:
Phase 1 shipped in commit f67db7d and release v2.3.0. The same boundary is present in v2.8.0.

Component Verified v2.8.0 behavior llm_providers.base Defines the runtime-checkable LLMProvider protocol and LLMProviderConfigurationError. llm_providers.registry Registers provider classes by name and creates one cached instance per provider name. Built-in providers Registers local, ollama, and mock with the core package. Optional LiteLLM provider Registers litellm only when its SDK imports successfully. Entry-point discovery Loads the zettelforge.llm_providers entry-point group during package import. A failed third-party load is logged at debug level and does not stop core startup. Public LLM client Resolves the configured provider, delegates generation, applies fallback rules, and exposes reload() for configuration changes.

docs.title: Failure and reload behavior
docs.text:
The public client treats missing SDKs, invalid provider names, and LLMProviderConfigurationError as configuration failures and raises them. It does not replace a permanent configuration problem with output from a different backend.

For other provider exceptions, the client tries the configured fallback. When you leave the fallback empty and select local, it retains the historical local to ollama fallback. If both recoverable paths fail, generation returns an empty string.

The registry caches constructed providers. After you change environment variables or configuration at runtime, llm_client.reload() clears cached configuration and provider instances. It preserves provider registrations.

docs.title: Phase status
docs.text:
Phase Original scope Verified outcome 1 Provider protocol, registry, built-ins, configuration plumbing, and extension discovery Shipped in v2.3.0; verified in v2.8.0 2 Dedicated OpenAI-compatible provider Superseded by RFC-012 3 Dedicated Anthropic provider Superseded by RFC-012 4 Provider configuration and third-party extension documentation Delivered through the current reference and extension guide 5 Per-call provider override Not implemented in v2.8.0

RFC-012 chose one optional litellm adapter instead of separate cloud-provider files. The v2.8.0 public generate() signature has no provider parameter. Each call resolves the process-wide configuration; reload() lets the process adopt a configuration change, but one call cannot select its own provider.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
• Extraction, update, classification, enrichment, evolution, and synthesis code use one generation boundary.
  • The core install does not require LiteLLM or a cloud-provider SDK.
  • Tests use the deterministic mock provider without a model service.
  • Third-party packages integrate through package metadata instead of modifying the repository.
  • Configuration failures remain visible at the point of use.

docs.title: Trade-offs
docs.text:
• Provider instances are process-wide singletons by name, and constructor options after the first lookup are ignored until reset. You call reload() before expecting runtime configuration changes to take effect.
  • Entry-point load failures appear only in debug logs, so plugin diagnostics require debug logging.
  • The protocol is synchronous and has no streaming method.
  • You cannot route individual calls to different providers through generate() in v2.8.0.

docs.title: Make LiteLLM a core dependency
docs.text: Rejected for the core install. ZettelForge keeps LiteLLM behind the litellm optional dependency so offline and local-only users do not install its dependency tree.

docs.title: Use the OpenAI SDK as the universal client
docs.text: Rejected. It would make one vendor SDK part of the core boundary and would not provide the same multi-provider coverage as the optional LiteLLM adapter.

docs.title: Require an abstract base class
docs.text: Rejected. A runtime-checkable protocol provides the required interface without forcing third-party providers to inherit from a ZettelForge class.

docs.title: Create one configuration section per provider
docs.text: Rejected. One llm section with a provider discriminator keeps provider selection in one place and avoids adding a top-level section for every adapter.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Accepted on 2026-04-16. ZettelForge keeps the Phase 1 provider boundary. RFC-012 supersedes the dedicated cloud adapters proposed in Phases 2 and 3. Phase 5 remains unimplemented in v2.8.0 and is not current behavior.

docs.title: RFC-003: Read-Path Depth Routing
docs.text:
Field Value Author Patrick Roland Status Draft — adversarial review completed, changes requested Created 2026-04-16 Last updated 2026-07-27 ZettelForge version v2.7.0 (design only; not implemented) Related RFCs RFC-001 Conversational Entity Extractor · RFC-002 Universal LLM Provider Interface

Not implemented

RFC-003 is a design proposal. Re-verified on 2026-07-27 against ZettelForge v2.7.0: none of the proposed modules (quality_gate.py, query_profile.py, query_markers.py, retrieval/) exist in the codebase and config.default.yaml has no recall.depth_routing section. The current recall() runs the uniform System 1 pipeline on every query. This page documents the proposal and its review status.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
recall() applies the same retrieval pipeline to every query regardless of complexity. The v2.7.0 benchmark report records these historical baseline numbers from a DGX Spark ARM64 run:

  • CTI single-entity lookups: p50 111 ms, p95 ~200 ms, ~75% accuracy
  • LOCOMO multi-hop long-horizon: p50 1,240 ms, p95 2,282 ms
  • Intent classification (keyword path): < 1 ms

Two failure modes follow from these numbers.

Low-complexity queries overpay. A query like CVE-2024-1234 triggers the full pipeline — intent classification, entity extraction, vector retrieval, graph traversal at depth 2, entity-augmented pull, and cross-encoder reranking — when a single entity-index lookup would answer it. The historical CTI p50 is inflated by phases that contribute no signal for this query class.

High-complexity queries hit a ceiling. Multi-hop CTI attribution (for example, "which threat actor used CVE-2024-3400 in campaigns that targeted healthcare between Q3 2024 and Q1 2025?") requires crossing 3+ entity boundaries with temporal constraints. The current top-k blend (default k=10) with depth-2 graph traversal cannot guarantee coverage of the full causal chain. Notes that are individually low-similarity but collectively form the answer are dropped before reranking. This explains the 25% accuracy gap on CTI and the long-tail p95 on LOCOMO.

The 5-way intent classifier already identifies these query classes but only weights traversal policy, not depth.

docs.title: Proposal
docs.text:
Introduce a Quality Gate on recall() that routes queries to one of two retrieval depths:

  • System 1 — the current blended-retrieval pipeline (fast, unchanged)
  • System 2 — a new exhaustive-scan path with pre-filtering and temporal-chunk scoring

The gate is deterministic, LLM-free on the fast path, and uses heuristic signals from the already-computed intent classification and entity extraction plus one additional cheap probe (vector top-1 score). A D-Mem (arXiv:2603.18631) finding grounds the approach: its multi-dimensional quality gate recovers 96.7% of full-deliberation performance while reducing computational cost.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
recall(query, ...)
  │
  ▼
IntentClassifier.classify(query)        # Existing — unchanged, <1ms
  │
  ▼
QueryProfile                            # New — cheap feature bundle
  ├─ intent + confidence
  ├─ query entities (from EntityExtractor)
  ├─ span markers (temporal, causal, multi-hop)
  └─ aggregation markers
  │
  ▼
QualityGate.route(profile) ──────┐      # New — deterministic, <5ms
  │                              │
  │ System 1                     │ System 2
  ▼                              ▼
System1Retriever          System2Retriever
= current recall() body   = candidate pre-filter
  (unchanged)               + temporal chunking
  │                         + chunk scoring
  │                         + within-chunk rerank
  │                              │
  └─── results ── upgrade? ──────┘
  │   (if System 1 score floor breached)
  ▼
List[MemoryNote]

docs.title: Gate design: additive bounded scoring
docs.text:
The gate computes a score ∈ [0.0, 1.0] from cheap features. Queries above system2_threshold (default 0.70) route to System 2; the rest stay on System 1.

Signal Weight CAUSAL intent prior +0.35 RELATIONAL intent prior +0.20 EXPLORATORY intent prior +0.20 TEMPORAL intent prior +0.10 Ambiguous intent (confidence < 0.4) +0.15 Multi-hop span markers +0.25 Temporal span markers +0.20 Causal chain markers +0.25 Aggregation markers +0.30 Comparison markers +0.15 Entity count ≥ 3 +0.10 Entity type count ≥ 2 +0.05

A fast-path shortcut forces System 1 unconditionally when: FACTUAL intent + entity count ≤ 1 + no multi-hop markers + no aggregation markers.

docs.title: System 2 pipeline
docs.text:
Where System 1 scores and ranks individual notes, System 2 scores temporal chunks to catch "collectively true, individually weak" patterns.

QueryProfile
  │
  ▼
1. CandidateFilter (entity-index expansion + 1-hop KG neighbors
                    + time-window expansion + vector top-200 fallback)
  │ target: 200–500 candidates
  ▼
2. TemporalChunker (sort by created_at, bucket by hourly|daily|weekly)
  │
  ▼
3. ChunkScorer (coverage 0.30 + density 0.20 + causal 0.20
               + centrality 0.15 + recency 0.15)
  │ select top-M chunks (default 5)
  ▼
4. Within-chunk rerank (cross-encoder on selected chunks only,
                        same as System 1 but bounded to ~100 pairs)
  │
  ▼
List[MemoryNote] (deduped, capped at k)

docs.title: Upgrade path
docs.text:
After System 1 completes, a second check can escalate to System 2 without re-running the gate:

  • Top vector score falls below system1_confidence_floor (default 0.40), or
  • CAUSAL/EXPLORATORY query returns fewer than 3 results

A config knob max_upgrade_rate (default 15%) caps the fraction of queries that upgrade in a rolling 100-query window. Chronic upgrades indicate the threshold is set too conservatively.

docs.title: Public API: no change
docs.text: recall(query, domain, k, include_links, exclude_superseded, include_expired) keeps its current signature and return type. Gate decisions appear in structured logs as gate_depth, gate_score, and gate_reasons.

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
Ships disabled by default. To opt in after upgrading to the version that delivers this RFC:

# config.yaml
recall:
  depth_routing:
    enabled: true

    quality_gate:
      system2_threshold: 0.70        # fraction [0,1]; lower → more System 2
      system1_confidence_floor: 0.40 # upgrade if top score < this
      max_upgrade_rate: 0.15         # cap upgrade rate in rolling window

    system2:
      max_candidates: 500
      chunk_size: auto               # auto | hourly | daily | weekly
      max_chunks: 5
      chunk_weights:
        coverage: 0.30
        density: 0.20
        causal: 0.20
        centrality: 0.15
        recency: 0.15

docs.title: New storage primitives
docs.text:
System 2 requires three new read methods on StorageBackend:

def get_entity_neighbors(
    self, etype: str, evalue: str, hop: int = 1, max_notes: int = 100,
) -> list[MemoryNote]: ...

def iterate_notes_in_range(
    self, start: str, end: str,
) -> Iterator[MemoryNote]: ...

def get_entity_degree(self, etype: str, evalue: str) -> int: ...

The proposal intends these to be SQLite read queries over existing note, KG, and entity indexes. The revised RFC still needs to prove the exact query plans before keeping the "no schema migrations required" claim.

docs.title: Adversarial review
docs.text: An adversarial review completed on 2026-04-16 returned REQUEST CHANGES with 4 blockers and 13 warnings.

docs.title: Open review findings after the 2026-07-27 re-audit
docs.text:
B1. Motivating example misroutes to System 1. The query "which threat actor used CVE-2024-3400 in campaigns targeting healthcare between Q3 2024 and Q1 2025?" scores 0.40 under the proposed weights — below the 0.70 threshold. The pattern \bused by .+ (?:to|in|for|against)\b does not match "used CVE". The query that RFC-003 was designed to fix routes to the path it already fails on.

B2. meta["top_vector_score"] does not exist. The upgrade path reads this key, but no current API exposes that metadata object. VectorRetriever.retrieve() can return (MemoryNote, score) tuples when called with return_scores=True; the revised RFC still needs to define where the top score is carried into the post-System-1 upgrade check.

B3. System 2 will bust the 800 ms budget if LLM NER is used. Current recall() query extraction calls extract_all() with its default use_llm=False, so the shipped read path is regex-only. The proposed System 2 candidate filter still needs to pin candidate-note extraction to regex-only behavior so future implementation does not call the LLM NER path across 200–500 notes.

B4. The storage contract is still underspecified. SQLite now has indexes on notes.created_at, KG edge endpoints, and entity lookup columns, but the three proposed StorageBackend methods do not exist. The revised RFC needs to specify exact queries and any incidence-count index required for get_entity_degree().

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Status: Draft — changes requested. Implementation remains deferred pending a revised RFC that resolves the findings above. See the adversarial review document for the full list of warnings and recommended fixes.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text: No migration is needed today because this RFC has not shipped. The verified v2.7.0 recall() path remains the uniform blended retrieval path. When the implementation lands, the gate ships disabled by default (enabled: false); existing deployments require no config changes to preserve current behavior.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Alternative Verdict LLM-based router Rejected — adds 300–500 ms to every query; non-deterministic; LLM-free fast path is an explicit constraint Learned classifier router Rejected for this RFC — no labeled dataset exists; deferred to a follow-up RFC once telemetry accumulates Always-System-2 Rejected — 7× latency regression on the dominant query class Depth as explicit recall() argument Rejected as sole mechanism — agents cannot reliably decide depth without gate heuristics Deeper graph traversal in System 1 Rejected — traversal cost is exponential; does not address "collectively true, individually weak" pattern

docs.title: RFC-012: LiteLLM Unified Provider
docs.text:
RFC-012 records why ZettelForge uses one optional LiteLLM adapter for cloud-hosted generation instead of maintaining a separate adapter for every model provider. Phase 1 shipped in v2.5.0 and remains implemented in v2.8.0. The upstream RFC still records its formal decision as pending.

Use this design record to understand the architecture and its consequences. For current keys, defaults, and provider examples, use the Configuration reference.

Field Value Author Patrick Roland Status Implemented — Phase 1; formal RFC decision pending Created 2026-04-25 Last verified 2026-08-14 Verified release ZettelForge v2.8.0 Related RFC RFC-002 Universal LLM Provider Interface Related ticket ZF-012

docs.title: Implementation status
docs.text: Scope Verified v2.8.0 state LiteLLM provider class and registry entry Implemented; first shipped in v2.5.0 Optional litellm dependency extra Implemented with a lower bound of litellm>=1.60.0 Per-call provider or model override Not implemented; the public generation function has no provider or model parameter Provider-specific llm.extra passthrough Not implemented; the client passes the values to the constructor, where this provider ignores unrecognized keyword arguments Embeddings through LiteLLM Outside this RFC; ZettelForge uses its embedding provider path instead

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
RFC-002 introduced a provider boundary so extraction, classification, enrichment, and synthesis use one generation function. Dedicated adapters for every hosted model service would duplicate authentication, request conversion, retry behavior, and dependency management.

The design needed to add hosted-model routing without making LiteLLM a dependency of the core ZettelForge installation. It also needed to preserve the existing synchronous generation contract used by the rest of the codebase.

docs.title: Proposal
docs.text:
Add litellm as a provider name beside local, ollama, and mock. The adapter converts the ZettelForge generation call into a litellm.completion() call. LiteLLM then selects its backend from the configured model identifier.

Keep the SDK in the optional zettelforge[litellm] dependency group. A local-only ZettelForge installation does not install LiteLLM.

docs.title: Provider boundary
docs.text:
LiteLLMProvider implements the same generate() shape as the other ZettelForge providers. It builds a chat message list and passes the configured model, token limit, temperature, timeout, and retry count to litellm.completion().

The adapter adds api_key only when you configure a non-empty key. In JSON mode, it adds response_format={"type": "json_object"}. It strips surrounding whitespace from the returned message content.

The adapter also sets LiteLLM's suppress_debug_info flag during the completion call and restores the previous value afterward, including when the call raises an exception. This keeps the change scoped to ZettelForge's call.

docs.title: Registration and dependency loading
docs.text:
ZettelForge imports the provider module and registers the name litellm during provider initialization. The provider module imports the LiteLLM SDK only when generation starts.

This lazy import has an important consequence: available() includes litellm even when the SDK is absent. A missing SDK raises an actionable ImportError when generation starts. Treat the registry list as a list of known provider names, not an installation check.

docs.title: Defaults have two layers
docs.text:
The provider class uses these constructor fallbacks when a caller supplies no values:

Constructor value Class fallback Model gpt-4o-mini API key empty string Timeout 60.0 seconds Retry count 2

Normal application calls load the shared llm configuration first. ZettelForge v2.8.0 defines qwen3.5:9b as the shared model default and 180.0 seconds as the shared timeout, then passes those values to the selected provider. Selecting provider: litellm without choosing a compatible model therefore does not activate the provider class's gpt-4o-mini fallback.

docs.title: Failure and fallback behavior
docs.text:
The adapter logs a failed completion and re-raises the exception. The public ZettelForge client then applies these rules:

  • A missing SDK or provider configuration error reaches the caller. ZettelForge does not hide it with a fallback.
  • Another completion exception invokes the explicitly configured fallback provider.
  • Without an explicit fallback, a failed LiteLLM completion returns an empty string from the public generation function.
  • The historical implicit fallback applies only from local to ollama; it does not add LiteLLM to that chain.

docs.title: extra does not reach LiteLLM completion
docs.text:
The shared client merges llm.extra into provider constructor arguments. LiteLLMProvider accepts unrecognized constructor arguments for registry compatibility and discards them. Values such as drop_params therefore do not reach litellm.completion() in v2.8.0.

Adding provider-specific completion arguments requires a source change or a future explicit passthrough design. Do not treat llm.extra as a LiteLLM request-parameter channel in this release.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
• ZettelForge keeps one generation boundary while LiteLLM owns backend-specific request routing.
  • Local and Ollama users avoid the optional cloud-routing dependency.
  • Existing generation call sites require no LiteLLM-specific branches.
  • The adapter preserves the shared logging and fallback boundary.

docs.title: Trade-offs
docs.text:
• LiteLLM compatibility and model naming remain upstream concerns.
  • The registry name does not prove the optional SDK is installed.
  • You select one process-wide provider and model configuration; individual calls cannot choose another model.
  • Provider-specific LiteLLM completion options cannot travel through llm.extra in v2.8.0.
  • The interface is synchronous and does not expose streaming through this provider boundary.

docs.title: Maintain one adapter per hosted provider
docs.text: Rejected. Separate OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Bedrock, and Vertex adapters would multiply authentication paths, dependencies, and tests inside ZettelForge.

docs.title: Make LiteLLM a core dependency
docs.text: Rejected. The optional dependency keeps the core and local-only installation smaller and avoids installing a cloud-routing SDK for readers who do not use it.

docs.title: Replace model-based routing with provider-specific configuration fields
docs.text: Rejected for Phase 1. The implemented adapter sends one model identifier to LiteLLM and leaves backend selection inside that SDK.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The formal decision remains pending in the v2.8.0 upstream RFC. The shipped code implements the Phase 1 direction: ZettelForge keeps LiteLLM optional, registers one adapter, and routes generation through the shared provider boundary.

That implementation does not constitute approval of the unshipped scope. Per-call model selection, LiteLLM-specific extra passthrough, and embedding support remain outside the implemented decision.

docs.title: Quickstart: your first memory
docs.text:
You will stand up a working ZettelForge instance, store three pieces of threat intelligence about APT28 and Lazarus Group, and recall them by natural-language query and by actor name. The whole path runs locally with no cloud account and no API keys.

What you learn

  • Storing CTI facts with remember()
  • Recalling notes with recall() (blended vector plus graph retrieval)
  • Looking up an actor directly with recall_actor()

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.10 or newer
  • Git and an internet connection for the clone, Python packages, and initial embedding-model download

The tutorial runs embeddings in-process and stores your notes in a local SQLite database plus a LanceDB vector index. You do not need Docker, TypeDB, Ollama, or an API key.

docs.title: Step 1: Install ZettelForge
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install it into a virtual environment.

git clone https://github.com/rolandpg/zettelforge.git
cd zettelforge
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .

The virtual environment keeps ZettelForge isolated from your system packages. It also avoids the externally managed Python restriction used by current Debian and Ubuntu releases.

Confirm the install:

python -c "import zettelforge; print(zettelforge.__version__)"

You see the installed version:

2.8.0

docs.title: Step 2: Keep this run offline
docs.text:
The base package enables optional LLM enrichment by default. Disable that slow path for this tutorial so ZettelForge does not try to contact an Ollama server:

export ZETTELFORGE_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED=false

Keep this shell open for the remaining steps.

docs.title: Step 3: Store and recall your first memories
docs.text:
The embedding model downloads automatically the first time you construct a MemoryManager. This is a one-time download; subsequent runs load it from cache.

Create a file called quickstart.py with the following content. The CTI facts and example.com references are synthetic tutorial data.

from zettelforge import MemoryManager

mm = MemoryManager()

note1, status1 = mm.remember(
    "APT28 (Fancy Bear) deployed a modified X-Agent implant against "
    "Ukrainian government networks in March 2026. The implant used "
    "CVE-2025-21298 for initial access via spearphishing attachments.",
    source_type="report",
    source_ref="https://example.com/apt28-ukraine-2026",
    domain="cti",
)

note2, status2 = mm.remember(
    "Lazarus Group conducted Operation DreamJob targeting defense "
    "contractors in South Korea and Japan during Q1 2026. The campaign "
    "used trojanized job offer PDFs delivering the DreamJob backdoor "
    "via LinkedIn messages.",
    source_type="report",
    source_ref="https://example.com/lazarus-dreamjob-2026",
    domain="cti",
)

note3, status3 = mm.remember(
    "APT28 was also observed using Cobalt Strike beacons for lateral "
    "movement after initial X-Agent deployment. The beacons called back "
    "to infrastructure hosted on bulletproof providers in Moldova.",
    source_type="report",
    source_ref="https://example.com/apt28-cobalt-strike",
    domain="cti",
)

print(f"Stored: {status1}, {status2}, {status3}")

print("\nQuery recall:")
results = mm.recall("What tools does APT28 use?", domain="cti", k=5)
for note in results:
    print(f"- {note.content.source_ref}")

print("\nActor recall:")
apt28_notes = mm.recall_actor("APT28", k=5)
for note in sorted(apt28_notes, key=lambda item: item.content.source_ref):
    print(f"- {note.content.source_ref}")

docs.title: Step 4: Run the tutorial
docs.text:
Run the file from the same shell:

python quickstart.py

The verified run produced this standard output:

Stored: created, created, created

Query recall:
- https://example.com/apt28-cobalt-strike
- https://example.com/apt28-ukraine-2026
- https://example.com/lazarus-dreamjob-2026

Actor recall:
- https://example.com/apt28-cobalt-strike
- https://example.com/apt28-ukraine-2026

remember() returns a (MemoryNote, status) tuple. The three created statuses confirm that the write path accepted each note. recall() blends vector and graph retrieval; the verified query ranks both APT28 notes before the unrelated Lazarus note. recall_actor() performs a direct entity-index lookup and returns the two notes indexed under the canonical actor name.

On the verified 2.8.0 build, startup also writes warnings to standard error for unset optional TypeDB credentials and the current FastEmbed model revision. Those warnings do not stop the SQLite tutorial.

Why the fast path matters

This tutorial disables optional LLM enrichment, but the core write path still embeds the note, writes it to SQLite and LanceDB, extracts heuristic entities, and updates heuristic graph edges. LLM causal extraction, richer entity extraction, and note evolution stay outside this success path.

Current offline lookup boundary

Use canonical actor labels such as APT28 for this tutorial. In the verified offline run, recall_cve("CVE-2025-21298") returned its note, but recall_actor("Fancy Bear"), recall_actor("Lazarus Group"), and recall_tool("Cobalt Strike") returned no matches. Configure and verify LLM enrichment before relying on alias or richer tool-name lookup. See the Configuration reference.

docs.title: What you built
docs.text:
You now have a working ZettelForge instance with:

  • Three stored notes about APT28 and Lazarus Group activity, embedded and persisted to a local SQLite database and LanceDB vector index
  • Entity index entries for the canonical APT28 actor, the CVE, and several other heuristically extracted entities
  • Blended retrieval that combines vector similarity with graph traversal and ranks both APT28 notes first for the tutorial query

The tutorial data lives under ~/.amem by default in zettelforge.db and the vectordb/ directory. The verified run completed the core flow without an external service.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Synthesize answers from memory. Configure an LLM before you depend on a model-generated answer. In the no-provider verification run, mm.synthesize(query, format="direct_answer") returned a structured fallback with confidence set to 0.0, not a model-generated synthesis. See the Configuration reference.
  • Ingest your first CTI report: chunk and store a long-form threat report with remember_report().
  • Memory Manager API reference: every public method, argument, and return shape.
  • Why the hybrid TypeDB plus LanceDB architecture: the design rationale behind blended retrieval.

ZettelForge is the open-source core documented on this site. ThreatRecall.ai is the hosted SaaS built on the same engine for teams that want managed recall without running infrastructure.

docs.title: Ingest your first CTI report
docs.text:
What you will build: A stored threat intelligence report with extracted CTI entities, queryable SQLite graph relationships, semantic recall, and a direct-answer synthesis call about APT28.

Time estimate: 15 minutes

Prerequisites:

  • You have completed Quickstart (Tutorial 01).
  • ZettelForge 2.7.0 is installed (pip install zettelforge).
  • An LLM provider is configured and running. Steps 3, 4, and 8 require LLM inference for full fact extraction and synthesis. Set ZETTELFORGE_LLM_PROVIDER and ZETTELFORGE_LLM_MODEL explicitly before you run this tutorial. Use an installed Ollama tag such as qwen2.5:3b, use local with Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GGUF and the matching GGUF file, or use litellm with the API key required by your hosted model.
  • ZettelForge uses SQLite by default. No external database required.

Verification state

This tutorial is in progress. On July 28, 2026, a verification run covered the SQLite runtime path, the no-LLM fallback, and the API shapes with a deterministic mock provider. A production LLM provider was not available in this environment, so LLM-generated wording, counts, and relationship richness are examples you verify against your provider before relying on them.

docs.title: Step 1: Start a Python session
docs.text:
Open a terminal and start a Python REPL.

python3

Import ZettelForge and create a MemoryManager instance.

from zettelforge import MemoryManager

mm = MemoryManager()

On the default SQLite backend, the manager initializes with no connection message. The storage backend is SQLiteBackend.

Note

This tutorial works with the default SQLite backend. If you set ZETTELFORGE_BACKEND=typedb, run TypeDB on localhost:1729 before you initialize the manager. Local SQLite graph traversal is capped at depth 2.

docs.title: Step 2: Create a sample threat report
docs.text:
Define a threat intelligence report as a Python string. This report describes APT28 using Cobalt Strike to exploit CVE-2024-1111 against the energy sector.

report = """
THREAT INTELLIGENCE REPORT: APT28 Campaign Targeting Energy Sector
Published: 2026-03-15
TLP:AMBER

Russian state-sponsored threat actor APT28 (also known as Fancy Bear) has been
observed conducting a sustained cyber espionage campaign against energy sector
organizations in Western Europe. The campaign, active since January 2026, leverages
Cobalt Strike beacons delivered through spear-phishing emails containing weaponized
PDF attachments.

Technical Analysis:
The initial access vector exploits CVE-2024-1111, a critical remote code execution
vulnerability in PDF rendering libraries (CVSS 9.8). Upon successful exploitation,
the payload deploys a Cobalt Strike beacon configured to communicate with C2
infrastructure hosted on compromised legitimate websites.

APT28 operators use Cobalt Strike's built-in lateral movement capabilities to
pivot through victim networks, targeting operational technology (OT) network
segments connected to SCADA systems. The threat actor has been observed
exfiltrating engineering schematics and network topology documents from
compromised energy utilities.

Indicators of Compromise:
- C2 Domain: update-service.energy-grid[.]com
- Cobalt Strike Beacon Hash: a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4
- Exploit Payload Hash: 9f8e7d6c5b4a9f8e7d6c5b4a9f8e7d6c
- Spear-phishing Subject: "Q1 2026 Energy Market Compliance Update"

MITRE ATT&CK Mapping:
- T1566.001 - Spear-phishing Attachment
- T1203 - Exploitation for Client Execution (CVE-2024-1111)
- T1071.001 - Web Protocols (Cobalt Strike C2)
- T1021.002 - SMB/Windows Admin Shares (Lateral Movement)

Recommendations:
Patch CVE-2024-1111 immediately. Block the listed IOCs at network perimeter.
Monitor for anomalous SMB traffic between IT and OT network segments.
"""

docs.title: Step 3: Ingest the report with remember_report()
docs.text:
Feed the report into ZettelForge. The remember_report() method chunks the text, runs two-phase LLM extraction on each chunk, and stores the results with CTI domain metadata.

Note

This step requires a configured LLM provider for the full tutorial output. If the LLM is unavailable, remember_report() stores a degraded fallback fact from the chunk and logs warnings; it does not produce the five extracted facts shown below. Start your provider before continuing.

results = mm.remember_report(
    content=report,
    source_url="https://intel.example.com/reports/apt28-energy-2026",
    published_date="2026-03-15",
    domain="cti",
    chunk_size=3000
)

The call returns a list of (note, status) tuples. Print the list in the next step to inspect the notes ZettelForge stored.

Tip

The output shows both phases in action. Phase 1 (extraction) pulls candidate facts and scores them by importance (1-10). Phase 2 (update) compares each fact against existing memory and decides ADD, UPDATE, or NOOP.

docs.title: Step 4: Inspect the extraction results
docs.text:
Print the results to see what ZettelForge created.

print(f"Total memory operations: {len(results)}\n")

for note, status in results:
    if note:
        print(f"[{status.upper()}] {note.id}")
        print(f"  Content:    {note.content.raw[:80]}...")
        print(f"  Domain:     {note.metadata.domain}")
        print(f"  Tier:       {note.metadata.tier}")
        print(f"  Importance: {note.metadata.importance}")
        print(f"  Keywords:   {note.semantic.keywords}")
        print(f"  Entities:   {note.semantic.entities}")
        print()

Representative output shape:

Total memory operations: 5

[ADDED] note_20260728_010541_ad4e
  Content:    APT28 uses Cobalt Strike beacons delivered through spear-phishing PDF attach...
  Domain:     cti
  Tier:       A
  Importance: 9
  Keywords:   ['uses', 'cobalt', 'strike', 'beacons', 'delivered', 'through', 'spear']
  Entities:   ['apt28', 'cobalt-strike']

[ADDED] note_20260728_010541_25e0
  Content:    CVE-2024-1111 is a critical remote code execution vulnerability in PDF rendering...
  Domain:     cti
  Tier:       A
  Importance: 9
  Keywords:   ['critical', 'remote', 'code', 'execution', 'vulnerability', 'rendering', 'libraries']
  Entities:   ['cve-2024-1111']

[ADDED] note_20260728_010542_50b4
  Content:    APT28 is conducting cyber espionage against Western European energy sector...
  Domain:     cti
  Tier:       A
  Importance: 8
  Keywords:   ['conducting', 'cyber', 'espionage', 'against', 'western', 'european', 'energy']
  Entities:   ['apt28']

[ADDED] note_20260728_010542_ef58
  Content:    APT28 targets operational technology and SCADA systems in energy utilities...
  Domain:     cti
  Tier:       A
  Importance: 8
  Keywords:   ['targets', 'operational', 'technology', 'scada', 'systems', 'energy', 'utilities']
  Entities:   ['apt28']

[ADDED] note_20260728_010542_316d
  Content:    C2 domain update-service.energy-grid.com is used by APT28 Cobalt Strike...
  Domain:     cti
  Tier:       A
  Importance: 7
  Keywords:   ['domain', 'update', 'service', 'energy', 'grid', 'used', 'cobalt']
  Entities:   ['apt28', 'cobalt-strike', 'update-service.energy-grid.com']

Note

Your note IDs and timestamps differ. A successful LLM pass returns one tuple per extracted fact; the sample fact set above produced five added tuples in the July 28, 2026 verification run. Without a working LLM provider, the same script produced one added fallback note for the whole chunk.

docs.title: Step 5: Query entity relationships from the knowledge graph
docs.text:
Check that ZettelForge built STIX entity relationships during ingestion. Use mm.get_entity_relationships() to query direct outgoing edges from an entity in the SQLite knowledge graph.

Note

APT-numbered groups (APT28, APT29, UNC series, FIN series) are indexed with entity_type="intrusion_set" by ZettelForge's entity extractor. Use "intrusion_set" as the entity type when querying them — "actor" returns a different (smaller) category.

actor_rels = mm.get_entity_relationships("intrusion_set", "apt28")
print("=== APT28 Relationships ===")
for rel in actor_rels:
    node = rel["node"]
    print(f"  APT28 --[{rel['relationship']}]--> {node['entity_type']}:{node['entity_value']}")

print()

tool_rels = mm.get_entity_relationships("tool", "cobalt-strike")
print("=== Cobalt Strike Relationships ===")
for rel in tool_rels:
    node = rel["node"]
    print(f"  Cobalt Strike --[{rel['relationship']}]--> {node['entity_type']}:{node['entity_value']}")

Observed output from the July 28, 2026 SQLite verification run:

=== APT28 Relationships ===
  APT28 --[USES_TOOL]--> tool:cobalt-strike
  APT28 --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010541_ad4e
  APT28 --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010542_50b4
  APT28 --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010542_ef58
  APT28 --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010542_316d

=== Cobalt Strike Relationships ===
  Cobalt Strike --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010541_ad4e
  Cobalt Strike --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010542_316d

Note

The SQLite path creates MENTIONED_IN edges and selected heuristic co-occurrence edges such as USES_TOOL. The July 28, 2026 verification run did not create explicit EXPLOITS_CVE or TARGETS_ASSET edges from this sample. Treat richer attack-chain edges as provider- and enrichment-dependent until you verify them in your environment.

docs.title: Step 6: Use recall() to find the ingested intel
docs.text:
Search memory using natural language. The recall() method blends vector similarity search with graph traversal.

results = mm.recall("APT28 cobalt strike energy sector", domain="cti", k=5)

print(f"Found {len(results)} relevant notes:\n")
for note in results:
    print(f"  [{note.id}] (importance={note.metadata.importance})")
    print(f"    {note.content.raw[:100]}...")
    print()

Observed output from the July 28, 2026 SQLite verification run:

Found 4 relevant notes:

  [note_20260728_010542_50b4] (importance=8)
    APT28 is conducting cyber espionage against Western European energy sector organizations...

  [note_20260728_010542_ef58] (importance=8)
    APT28 targets operational technology and SCADA systems in energy utilities...

  [note_20260728_010541_25e0] (importance=9)
    CVE-2024-1111 is a critical remote code execution vulnerability in PDF rendering...

  [note_20260728_010542_316d] (importance=7)
    C2 domain update-service.energy-grid.com is used by APT28 Cobalt Strike beacons...

docs.title: Step 7: Walk the relationship chain with traverse_graph()
docs.text:
Traverse the knowledge graph starting from APT28 to discover the full attack chain.

paths = mm.traverse_graph(start_type="intrusion_set", start_value="apt28", max_depth=2)

print(f"Graph traversal found {len(paths)} paths:\n")
for i, path in enumerate(paths):
    chain = []
    for step in path:
        if not chain:
            chain.append(f"{step['from_type']}:{step['from_value']}")
        chain.append(f"--[{step['relationship']}]--> {step['to_type']}:{step['to_value']}")
    print(f"  Path {i+1}: {' '.join(chain)}")

Observed output from the July 28, 2026 SQLite verification run:

Graph traversal found 8 paths:

  Path 1: intrusion_set:apt28 --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010542_ef58
  Path 2: intrusion_set:apt28 --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010542_50b4
  Path 3: intrusion_set:apt28 --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010542_316d
  Path 4: intrusion_set:apt28 --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010542_316d --[SUPERSEDES]--> note:note_20260728_010541_ad4e
  Path 5: intrusion_set:apt28 --[USES_TOOL]--> tool:cobalt-strike
  Path 6: intrusion_set:apt28 --[USES_TOOL]--> tool:cobalt-strike --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010542_316d
  Path 7: intrusion_set:apt28 --[USES_TOOL]--> tool:cobalt-strike --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010541_ad4e
  Path 8: intrusion_set:apt28 --[MENTIONED_IN]--> note:note_20260728_010541_ad4e

The USES_TOOL path shows APT28 connected to Cobalt Strike. This verification run did not produce an explicit path from APT28 to CVE-2024-1111 on the SQLite path.

docs.title: Step 8: Synthesize a threat brief
docs.text:
Use synthesize() to generate a direct-answer brief about APT28 from all ingested memory. The synthesis engine retrieves relevant notes, builds context, and produces a structured answer through the LLM.

Note

This step requires a configured LLM. Without an LLM, synthesis returns a confirmed fallback response: synthesis["answer"] = "No specific answer found...", synthesis["confidence"] = 0.0, synthesis["sources"] = []. Retrieval still runs, but the LLM answer is empty. This tutorial uses direct_answer; re-audit the other synthesis formats before you rely on them in production.

result = mm.synthesize(
    query="What do we know about APT28?",
    format="direct_answer",
    k=10
)

synthesis = result["synthesis"]
meta = result["metadata"]

print("=== APT28 Direct Answer ===\n")
print(synthesis["answer"])
print(f"\nConfidence: {synthesis['confidence']}")
print(f"\nSources used: {meta['sources_count']}")
print(f"Model: {meta['model_used']}")
print(f"Latency: {meta['latency_ms']}ms")

Output shape (requires a working LLM provider):

=== APT28 Direct Answer ===

<LLM-generated answer grounded in the retrieved notes>

Confidence: <float between 0 and 1>

Sources used: <number of retrieved notes>
Model: qwen2.5:3b
Latency: <milliseconds>ms

docs.title: What you built
docs.text:
You ingested a raw threat intelligence report and turned it into structured, queryable knowledge:

  1. Chunked ingestion -- remember_report() split the report and ran two-phase LLM extraction on each chunk
  2. Fact extraction -- The sample fact set produced five scored facts with a configured provider; the fallback path produced one degraded chunk-level note when the provider was unavailable
  3. Entity indexing -- The entity index records values such as intrusion_set:apt28, tool:cobalt-strike, cve:cve-2024-1111, and domain:update-service.energy-grid.com when those entities appear in extracted facts
  4. Relationship query -- get_entity_relationships() retrieves direct KG edges for any entity
  5. Graph traversal -- traverse_graph() walks the available relationship paths from an entity
  6. Semantic recall -- recall() blends vector similarity and graph traversal for ranked retrieval
  7. Synthesis -- synthesize() generates an LLM-backed answer grounded in your stored intelligence

docs.title: LLM quick reference
docs.text:
This section is for LLM agents consuming ZettelForge's CTI ingestion pipeline programmatically.

Ingest a report -- mm.remember_report(content, source_url, published_date, domain="cti", chunk_size=3000). Returns List[Tuple[Optional[MemoryNote], str]] where each tuple is (note, status) and status is one of "added", "updated", "corrected", "noop". Chunks on sentence boundaries, runs Phase 1 fact extraction (LLM scores importance 1-10, filters by min_importance=3), then Phase 2 update decisions (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP against existing memory). Default max_facts=10 per chunk. Requires LLM for multi-fact extraction. If the provider is unavailable, the current fallback stores one degraded fact from the chunk.

Recall intel -- mm.recall(query, domain="cti", k=10). Returns List[MemoryNote] ranked by blended vector + graph score. Superseded notes are excluded by default. For entity-specific lookup: mm.recall_entity(entity_type, entity_value) where entity_type is one of the indexed entity buckets, including cve, intrusion_set, actor, tool, campaign, attack_pattern, domain, url, md5, sha1, and sha256. Shortcuts: mm.recall_cve("CVE-2024-1111"), mm.recall_actor("apt28"), mm.recall_tool("cobalt-strike").

Query entity relationships -- mm.get_entity_relationships(entity_type, entity_value). Returns List[Dict] where each item has node (dict with entity_type, entity_value), relationship (str), edge_properties (dict), and note_id (str). Writes to the SQLite KG during remember() and remember_report().

Traverse the graph -- mm.traverse_graph(start_type, start_value, max_depth=2). Returns List[List[Dict]] -- a list of paths, each path a list of steps. Each step has from_type, from_value, relationship, to_type, to_value. Depth is capped at 2 in the local SQLite path. Valid start_type values include intrusion_set, actor, tool, cve, campaign, asset, and note. APT-numbered groups (APT28, UNC series) are indexed as intrusion_set, not actor. The July 28, 2026 SQLite tutorial run observed USES_TOOL, MENTIONED_IN, and SUPERSEDES relationships.

Synthesize a brief -- mm.synthesize(query, format="direct_answer", k=10). Returns dict with top-level keys query, format, synthesis, metadata, sources. For "direct_answer": synthesis["answer"] (str), synthesis["confidence"] (float 0-1), synthesis["sources"] (list). ZettelForge exposes additional synthesis formats in source, but this tutorial only verifies direct_answer. Requires LLM for non-fallback output.

MemoryNote fields -- id (str), content.raw (str), semantic.keywords (list), semantic.entities (list), metadata.domain (str), metadata.tier (str, A/B/C), metadata.importance (int 1-10), metadata.confidence (float), links.superseded_by (optional str), links.supersedes (list).

Configuration -- Set ZETTELFORGE_LLM_PROVIDER and ZETTELFORGE_LLM_MODEL explicitly before you run extraction. The July 28, 2026 source checkout has hardcoded Ollama-oriented fallback values in LLMConfig, a config.default.yaml sample with an unresolved Ollama model placeholder, and a root config.yaml that selects litellm with nvidia/meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct. The verification run did not confirm the sample placeholder as a working upstream model tag. To run fully offline, set ZETTELFORGE_LLM_PROVIDER=local, use Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GGUF, and set the matching GGUF filename in provider extra options. Default embedding is nomic-embed-text-v1.5-Q via fastembed (in-process). Environment overrides: ZETTELFORGE_LLM_MODEL, ZETTELFORGE_LLM_PROVIDER, ZETTELFORGE_LLM_URL, ZETTELFORGE_LLM_API_KEY, TYPEDB_HOST, TYPEDB_PORT, TYPEDB_DATABASE.
